#2678. Wrestling Preview: #1 Penn State at #13 Oklahoma

The Nittany Lions hit the road for the first time this young season, reciprocating Oklahoma's trip to the Bryce Jordan Center last fall. Let's hope the Sooners field closer to their starting lineup this year than they did last – it would be far more surprising if they send out backups on their home mat, but weirder things have happened.

Penn State wrestling raised the 2026 championship banner on Thursday night and started off the season with a thrashing of in-state foe Bloomsburg, who only won one of the ten bouts (against likely the third option at 141, hometown grappler and coach's son Hayden Cunningham). The first dual of the year saw the folkstyle debut of world champion (and local State College celebrity) Masanosuke Ono and the return to competition for all American Tyler Kasak, as well as the other usual suspects from last year's championship squad.

They take on an Oklahoma team that frankly feels under ranked to me, especially with a pair of transfers that will be familiar names for PSU fans in Paddy Gallagher and Brian Soldano. As of the writing of this preview, the Sooners' most recent outing was a 9-win drubbing of future PSU opponent Northern Colorado, who won their only bout against an OU backup at 165.

This should be a fun early test for the Lions, who look to settle down and get everyone in mid-season form already after a handful of bouts were closer than some hoped in their last outing.

#1 – Luke Lilledahl (Jr., St Charles, MO)

Sebastian Degennaro (So., Port Lucie, FL) OR#15 – Conrad Hendrikson (Jr., Carollton, TX)

Masanosuke Ono (Sr., Matsue City, Japan) ORNate Desmond (So., Bethlehem, PA)

#3 – Marcus Blaze (So., Perrysburg, OH) ORHayden Cunningham (Jr., State College, PA)

#4 – Shayne Van Ness (Sr., Somerville, NJ)

#16 – Rafael Hipolito (Sr., Manaus, Brazil)

Owen Eck (Jr., Andale, KS) OR#7 – Paddy Gallagher (Sr., Chesterland, OH)

#1 – Mitchell Mesenbrink (Sr., Hartland, WI)

Mason Ontiveros (Fr., Turlock, CA) OR#10 – Brian Soldano (Sr., Wantage, NJ)

Lilledahl majored Hendriksen when the two faced off last year and is the OU wrestler listed in intermat's rankings, but Degennaro got the start in Oklahoma's last outing, beating a UNC ranked wrestler. I still can't Bear to make a prediction different than last year's result, though.

Masa Ono started off with a bang but seemingly got himself over excited in his PSU singlet debut – just a takedown shy of a tech fall in the first period, he slowed down a lot in the final two periods and ended up getting taken down himself before settling for a major decision. This bout could either be a tech fall in the first, or a close decision in the third. I'm not sure it would be anything in between – so I'm going to go conservative.

With Marcus Blaze still out and Nate Desmond seemingly staying at 133 until the end of the year, this looks like, rather than my prediction of Herring, this might be Casey's oldest again. His opponent this bout is even tougher, and points will be harder for Hayden to score. Oklahoma's best shot will probably mean bonus for the hometown team.

Shayne got the season's first pin, and he looked smooth doing it. I have a feeling he's going to approach this season, likely his last, with a chip on his shoulder – especially since he's starting lower ranked than he's been in a few years. His final tour continues this night.

Tyler was back for the first time in over a season on Thursday, and got a very late takedown to make the score close to bonus. He seems to need some time to get back into the thick of things, and I think it'll take just a few more bouts for him to get his feel more under him.

PJ Duke looks in mid season form already, even up another weight. He always seemed to be a large 157er, so fits right in at this weight; he'll likely take on Ohio State transfer Paddy Gallagher, who teammate Mitchell Mesenbrink got bonus against three times last season. It's doubtful that the new coaching staff will have had much impact on Gallagher in this short period of time; he's still going to be a good wrestler, but PJ's at another level.

This is Mitchell Mesenbrink, and his baggy singlet. He'll get a tech fall, it's just a question of how fast he'll get it in.

Rutgers transfer Soldano hasn't yet wrestled this year; his young teammate is very good too, and will likely be ranked if the senior doesn't crack the lineup. Rocco #1 should win over either pretty easily if he's anywhere near where we expect him to be, but with a score just shy of bonus.

Josh Barr will quietly once again be the most consistently dominant wrestler on the Penn State squad. The wrestler that he's likely to face this weekend is ranked, but that doesn't mean much.

Connor weighed in under 230 pounds on Thursday, and will probably keep gaining, at least a little bit, as the season goes on. Hill should be a good test, but I expect Mirasola to dominate on the mat if not the scoreboard.

#2675. Aaron Rodgers Could Reach Significant NFL Milestone vs. Bengals

Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers is one win away from tying Drew Brees for the fourth-most career wins all time (including playoffs). Rodgers is currently at 180.

The only quarterbacks in NFL history who have won more starts are Tom Brady with 286 wins, Peyton Manning with 200 and Brett Favre with 199.

Rodgers needs four wins to surpass Brees (172) on the regular-season all-time win list. He would move into fourth all-time, behind Manning (186), Favre (186) and Brady (251). Rodgers has repeatedly stated that this season will be his final one, so he won't catch Manning and Favre.

With the Steelers' 34-22 win over the Indianapolis Colts in Week 5, Rodgers surpassed Ben Roethlisberger in career wins (166), moving into fifth place.

Rodgers' 4-yard touchdown pass to Darnell Washington against the New Orleans Saints in Week 7 was historic, as he surpassed Manning for third all-time in regular-season touchdown passes with 540.

Only Brady (649) and Brees (571) have thrown more touchdown passes.

Rodgers has now thrown 585 career TD passes (including postseason), the third most in NFL history. He surpassed Manning for that record in Week 5.

Rodgers surpassed Roethlisberger (64,088) on the career passing yards list last year. Rodgers now sits fifth all-time, while Roethlisberger dropped to seventh.

Rodgers needs 1,855 passing yards this season to reach the 70,000-yard milestone.

Against the Patriots, Goff is 1-3. That’s a 25-percent win rate.

#2671. Mavericks vs. Cavaliers Recap: Dallas struggles on the road, falls 127-117 to star-less Cavaliers

The Dallas Mavericks (7-6) fell to the Cleveland Cavaliers (7-7), 127-117 in a Saturday night matchup on the road. The matchup followed Dallas' 133-94 beatdown loss to the Minnesota Timberwolves on Thursday night. The Mavericks needed a bounce-back performance after Thursday night's blunder, and failed to take advantage of a second-string Cavaliers team.

Max Christie, Sergio de Larrea, Dereck Lively, and Tarik Biberovic were out for the Mavericks. Cleveland was without Donovan Mitchell, James Harden, Peyton Watson, Evan Mobley, Jarret Allen, and Sam Merrill. The Cavaliers sat all their top players after being unable to leave Miami until 9 a.m. due to a nationwide FAA grounding, following their 133-121 loss to the Heat. The nationwide grounding led to a call from Mitchell to cancel the game.

Kyrie Irving led the Mavericks with 34 points, six rebounds, and five assists, with 28 of those points coming in the second half. Tyrese Proctor contributed 24 points, 11 rebounds, and 10 assists, his first career triple-double, for the shorthanded Cavaliers.

The Mavericks struggled to defend the three early on, allowing Cleveland to make six threes in the first quarter, taking 58% of their shots from behind the arc. The Cavaliers, though shorthanded, had a hot hand early, allowing them to compete with the Mavericks in the first period. Caleb Martin was a bright spot for the Mavericks in this period, contributing nine first-quarter points as he continues to string together solid contributions in Dallas. Though the Mavericks couldn't stop Meleek Thomas's three-point shot early in the game, they walked into the second period at a 33-33 stalemate.

The Mavericks struggled offensively in the second period, letting their offensive mishaps affect how they defended the Cavaliers on the other end. The Cavaliers' early hot hand from behind the arc faded away in the second quarter, but they were able to go inside, as the Mavericks continued to struggle to defend them. The Mavericks needed more from Cooper Flagg in this quarter, who went 1-of-6 from the field as the Cavaliers' lead grew behind their 28-9 run in the quarter. Dallas walked into the intermission after giving up 38 points in the period, down 71-53, with a desperate need to punch back in the second half.

Dallas entered the second half uninspired to turn around its double-digit deficit, letting the lead swell to over twenty points. Dallas attempted to make a run midway through the third period, cutting the lead to 14, but continued to be unable to defend Cleveland to close the lead in any meaningful way. After a string of defensive stops, the Mavericks closed the gap with the Cavaliers, cutting the lead to 10. Irving provided a necessary 20 points in the third quarter when the Mavericks couldn't find a bucket. Even then, the Mavericks entered the fourth quarter with a 14-point deficit to dig themselves out of. The Mavericks' struggles seeped into the fourth quarter, despite everything Irving tried to do for Dallas. The Mavericks were unable to string together enough stops to fight back, falling 127-117.

Here are three takeaways from Saturday night's loss.

The Mavericks' offensive struggles continued on the road, shooting 39-of-94 from the field in the loss to Cleveland. Dallas needed someone to step up alongside Irving, but failed to take advantage of a less-talented group. This team needs more from guys like PJ Washington and Naji Marshall, who both shot poorly from the field in the loss to the Cavaliers. Off-nights from Flagg mean that someone else needs to answer the call, and the Mavericks failed to find someone to do so against Cleveland.

Cooper Flagg struggled in Saturday night's matchup with the Cavaliers, finishing with 18 points on 6-of-19 from the field. He was unable to find his shot tonight, and it felt like he was trying to force himself out of his slump by trying to draw whistles that he didn't get. He shot 0-of-6 from behind the arc tonight, though the Mavericks shot poorly from three as a whole. The Mavericks need more from Flagg, especially when facing a team missing its best players, because Irving can't be left to do it on his own. Flagg's youth showed tonight, and the Mavericks will need him to return to his All-Star-caliber self.

Kyrie Irving's 20-point third quarter gave the Mavericks a glimmer of temporary hope, with the Mavericks closing the Cavaliers' lead to 10. He was able to find his shot in this quarter, giving the Mavericks the push they needed to try to close the gap on the Cavaliers. Irving finished with 34 points, with the Mavericks needing every last one. Irving has played like an All-Star since returning from his ACL tear, and tonight was another impressive showing, coming when Dallas needed it the most. The Mavericks were unable to find anyone to step up to the plate alongside Irving and play with some shame against the Cleveland B-team.

The Mavericks are back in action Sunday, as they travel to Boston to face the Celtics at the TD Garden. Catch the tail end of the Mavericks back-to-back at 5 p.m. CT on KFAA-TV and MavsTV.

#2670. Mike the Tiger has seen enough: LSU mascot goes after Texas player after brutal loss

Immediately following LSU's heartbreaking last-second loss to Arch Manning and Texas, the Tigers' famed mascot (the costumed one, not the live animal who lives on the Baton Rouge campus) was seen briefly getting into it with a Texas football players in the game's aftermath.

Toppmeyer: Arch Manning can laugh about those 3 picks. There's nothing funny about Lane Kiffin's LSU

In a video captured by Hunter McMann of Baton Rouge TV station WBRZ, Texas football players can be seen heading to the end zone of Tiger Stadium to taunt the LSU student section. As the video progresses, it shows Longhorns running back Raleek Brown — who caught the game-winning touchdown — exchanging words with LSU linebacker Jake Ibieta.

The video concludes with Texas receiver Chris Stewart saying something to LSU's Mike the Tiger. Whatever Stewart said prompted Mike to try and confront the Longhorn, with a staff member getting between the two. Here's a look at the postgame video:

Frustrations are high in Baton Rouge amid a disappointing opening season for Lane Kiffin and Co. With the Tigers' fourth loss of the year, LSU is almost certainly eliminated from College Football Playoff contention.

What's more, the loss came after the Tigers led Texas since roughly the 10-minute mark of the second quarter. The LSU defense did its part to keep the Tigers in the game, picking off Manning three times. However, LSU quarterback Sam Leavitt also threw three interceptions, and the offense only produced one second-half scoring drive. The Tigers on offense threw an interception, scored a touchdown then punted four straight times in the second half.

The Tigers' remaining two games will be more for pride than CFP contention, with trips to No. 9 Tennessee and Arkansas ending the season. That means LSU fans' final memory of the season, from Tiger Stadium, at least, will feature yet another heartbreaking, frustrating conclusion.

One that even Mike the Tiger is fed up with.

#2667. Jakobe Thomas gave Kirk Cousins No. 8 for nothing (other than wins)

The Raiders arguably could have driven a harder bargain over the trade that sent quarterback Kirk Cousins back to the Vikings. Vikings safety Jakobe Thomas could have driven a harder bargain over the return of Cousins’s preferred number.

Thomas told reporters that he gave Cousins No. 8 without payment.

“No money needed,” Thomas said, via Ben Goessling of the Minneapolis Star Tribune. “I just need him to come here and win games. On the field, Miami looks to continue the momentum after a closer-than-it-really-was 36-25 win over Duke on Homecoming yesterday. That garbage time score cost Miami the cover of the spread (-13.5 to -14.5 depending on where you caught it) so it was "significant to some" as broadcasters like to joke.

For Virginia Tech, they're looking to both bounce back and play spoiler. Miami is every team's Super Bowl (yes, including you, Notre Dame), so that part doesn't need any elaboration. The other part is that Virginia Tech just lost at home by 3 touchdowns….TO STANFORD 40-22. The Cardinal raced out to a 21-0 lead in the first half thanks to a trio of VT turnovers: 2 interceptions thrown by QB Ethan Grunkermeyer and a lost fumble by a receiver after a hard hit during a tackle.

Virginia Tech finally scored to make it 21-7, but from there, the teams would more or less trade scores, leading to the final 40-22 score line. While credit is due to Stanford for dominating this game and earning the victory, this was an atrocious performance from Virginia Tech. That is part of the basis for this enormous opening line, but expect to receive VT's best efforts next weekend, both because we're Miami and that's what teams need to do when playing us, and VT is looking to rebound from the horrible embarrassment of the Stanford loss as well.

So while the emotional stakes are high for the Hokies, the tangible stakes for Miami are massive. A win clinches a spot in the ACC Championship Game, and keeps the momentum rolling forward.

You know the mentality: 1-0. So let's work and make that happen. And, hopefully, put up enough points to cover this massive spread so the game isn't close or stressful in the second half at all.

#2665. Nets were thrown into travel chaos during the FAA ground stop: ‘Something we couldn’t control’

MEMPHIS, Tenn. — The name of the game in the NBA is adjustments.

It's usually about adjusting to other teams. But for the Nets — and a host of others around the league over the past two days — it was adjusting their travel.

The Nets — who were en route to play the Grizzlies, an eventual 129-110 loss — got thrown into travel chaos Friday night and Saturday morning, just like the rest of the country. The Federal Aviation Administration's decision to ground every flight nationwide for hours Friday left travelers scrambling, and the Nets were among them.

"Yeah, I mean, obviously it was something that we couldn't control," Nets coach Jordi Fernández said. "And to be honest with you, it was not that bad. We had good rest and got here [Saturday] morning and did our walkthrough, and probably [would have] gone to the gym, but we were not able to. And I think we feel good and ready to go."

Brooklyn Nets head coach Jordi Fernandez looks on during the second half of an NBA basketball game in New Orleans, Wednesday, Nov. 11, 2026. AP Photo/Tyler Kaufman

The ground stop lasted over four hours before the FAA finally let airplanes take off Friday night. The Nets were one of five NBA teams that had been slated to fly that day for games Saturday.

Brooklyn had been coming off a dominant 142-111 victory over the Pelicans on Wednesday night at Smoothie King Arena. They had stayed in New Orleans and practiced in the city Friday morning before heading to the airport to charter to Memphis.

The Nets had just boarded their team plane in New Orleans, but had their flight halted in place. They eventually had to deboard the plane, scramble and find a hotel and stay overnight in New Orleans.

Eventually, the Nets flew out at about 9 a.m. Saturday and arrived around 11 a.m., though the times blurred to Fernández.

"Every day feels the same day and I just know the team that I play against in the city that I'm in," Fernández laughed. "I don't know about time, sorry."

The Nets had initially planned to have a morning shootaround in Memphis. But arriving that morning instead of the afternoon prior, their plans got changed.

They faced the Grizzlies later that night at FedExForum.

"Yeah, I mean, some of the guys we would have done some sort of shooting in the morning. It's been the routine that they've had so far, whether it's in a team setting or shooting times and walk-through and stuff like that. But we were not able to do it because of the time that we got here," Fernández said. "So, like I said, it's not ideal. We got here, everybody's safe. It's the most important thing."

CHECK OUT THE LATEST NBA STANDINGS AND NETS STATS

Nets play-by-play voice Chris Carrino and color analyst Tim Capstraw — Brooklyn's radio announcers for WFAN — were flying commercial and also got caught by the travel chaos. With direct transit from New Orleans to Memphis already all but impossible, the duo had flown to Houston and planned to catch a connecting flight but got stranded in Texas. They stayed in the airport and flew into Memphis on a 7:20 a.m. flight.

Ironically, the Grizzlies had also been in New Orleans, and beat the Pelicans on Friday night.

JetBlue and American Airlines planes sit at gates at Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport after the FAA lifted a ground stop in Washington, Nov. 14, 2026. REUTERS

Memphis had to fly home Saturday morning as well.

"Before the New Orleans game you could see a lot of chatter courtside and in the locker room about what was going to happen," Grizzlies coach Tuomas Iisalo said.

"We departed at maybe 11:30 when our original time was about 10 o'clock … instead of doing a morning shootaround on back-to-backs, a lot of times what teams do is a jog through here at the area, so you don't come back twice."

The ground stop played havoc with travel.

The Detroit Pistons had already flown to Miami, with the Chicago Bulls, Cleveland Cavaliers and Memphis Grizzlies all having played Friday night and been expected to fly afterward, according to ESPN.

Friday saw a total of 9,132 cancellations and 7,030 delays. Saturday saw thousands more, with the numbers still growing.

Officials cited "extraordinary circumstances" caused by communications issues at regional air traffic control centers for the stoppage.

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy pointed to "old switches, old routers."

The Nets had a jumbo lineup again Saturday, but not their leading scorer.

Michael Porter Jr. was out Saturday after being a late scratch due to personal reasons. But the backcourt was healthy, with Nolan Traore and Mikel Brown Jr. both returning after having missed the win in New Orleans.

The Nets went with Egor Dëmin, Danny Wolf, Noah Clowney, Julius Randle and Day'Ron Sharpe, every starter at least 6-foot-9, as they had been against the Pelicans. The Nets are the first team to do so since the Lakers on April 21, 1990.

#2664. Corey Levin is ready to be the Falcons’ starting center vs. Chiefs

The best offensive lines function as one. Chemistry is so important to the success of this position group, and it's most important for the center who's calling the protections.

This is why I was mildly surprised the Falcons shipped Ryan Neuzil off to the Ravens just before the trade deadline on Tuesday. The NFC South is a mess, every team is currently sitting with three wins, and winning the division is still very possible. Michael Penix Jr.'s early career and development have been disrupted by injury and Kirk Cousins, and switching out centers in the middle of the season doesn't seem like the smoothest path to his success.

You know who isn't worried about the chemistry with his teammates? New starting center Corey Levin. For Levin, it's all about building trust with his teammates.

"First and foremost, just proving to them that they can trust me with everything that they trusted Neuzil with," Levin said Wednesday. "And then, obviously, I'm a different player than Neuzil. We play our own style and things like that. So them getting comfortable with how I may do a certain thing or communicate a certain way — just building that as quick as possible, and we get plenty of reps of practice to do it. So we really have no excuse."

While Neuzil would have gotten the first-team practice reps to prepare for each opponent up to this week, the backup center does take some early reps with the starter in each practice and in warmups before each game. In the immortal words of legendary Falcons safety William Moore, "How am I supposed to get ready when I stay ready?" That's the goal for the backup center — to stay ready in case the next man up is needed. And now Levin is.

When asked about the differences between his play and Neuzil's, Levin noted the difference in their builds and athleticism.

"Like, he's extremely athletic, and I'm not saying I'm not athletic. But I might weigh a little bit more than him, so different ways to play center. And I try to emulate him when he's here, for the offense that we're running, and now that he's not here, just kind of doing… not entirely my way, but still within my way."

And now that Levin is the Falcons' starter, he got about 60 practice snaps per day with the starting offense in this week's practices to prepare for the Chiefs this week.

His teammates describe Levin as a high-energy, happy guy. His experience as an NFL journeyman certainly impacted that attitude.

"[I'm] just kind of always a positive, upbeat guy," he said. "I'm happy to come to work with a smile on my face. Just because I'm grateful. Like you said, I bounced around. I know what it looks like to not have exactly the situation you want to be in. So when you're in the building every day, it's a blessing.

Sunday's game against the Chiefs will be Levin's eighth NFL start. He's played 14 offensive snaps and 36 special teams snaps so far this season.

#2662. Nets sorely miss Michael Porter Jr. in beatdown by Grizzlies

MEMPHIS, Tenn. — The Nets came into Saturday with every advantage. And they flushed them all with an embarrassing 129-110 non-effort against the Grizzlies before 15,103 at FedExForum.

The Nets were the fresher, more rested team. They were coming off a huge win and a solid practice, while Memphis was coming off a back-to-back. And while they were missing Michael Porter Jr., the Grizzlies were without Ty Jerome, one of the biggest breakout stories in basketball.

And the Nets never competed. Not for a moment.

Brooklyn Nets center Day'Ron Sharpe (20) handles the ball against Memphis Grizzlies forward Cameron Boozer (27) on Saturday, Nov. 14, 2026, in Memphis, Tenn. AP Photo/Brandon Dill

"It's frustrating they played harder than us," admitted Jordi Fernández.

They were down by 18 in a first quarter that saw them give up 9-for-11 shooting from deep. They fell behind by as much as 26.

And when it was done, they knew they'd turned in a stinker.

"We cut it to seven at some point and you should've been in the game, but we're not mature enough," said a frustrated Fernández. "We played against a team that played on the second [night] of a back-to-back with the same travel that we had and they played the right way, played really hard. We're not there yet."

Sitting on the bench as a late scratch for personal reasons, Porter saw his Nets stumble badly right out of the gate, already trailing 35-17 with 2:47 left in the first quarter after a Cam Spencer 3-pointer.

After a sloppy turnover by Egor Dëmin, the Nets called a timeout. The young guard got chastised by Fernández and spoken to by Julius Randle.

Brooklyn Nets forward Julius Randle (30) shoots against the Memphis Grizzlies during an NBA basketball game Saturday, Nov. 14, 2026, in Memphis, Tenn. AP Photo/Brandon Dill

"I was just trying to tell, it's on us that we had bad organization getting the ball in," Randle said. "But in those moments, instead of turning the ball over and having a live turnover, just take the five-second [violation] so we can just get back and get our defense set. So, on us. Just trying not to compound it."

"Yeah, they've got to grow fast," Fernández said of young guards Dëmin, Nolan Traore and Mikel Brown Jr. "Being 20 is not an excuse. … I'm frustrated or I get mad because I know they're very good and they're better than this. And when I just don't see a connected group is when it hurts because we make those pushes and cut it to 10, cut it to seven. It's just frustrating."

The Nets had clawed to within 85-77 on Randle's 3 with 5:12 left in the third quarter, but they got no closer.

A Randle turnover killed the brittle Brooklyn momentum, and it quickly swung back the other way. The Nets coughed up a 16-1 run, with a Taylor Hendricks dunk putting them in a 101-78 hole with 40 seconds left in the third.

Brooklyn Nets head coach Jordi Fernandez gestures from the sideline during an NBA basketball game against the Memphis Grizzlies in Memphis, Tenn., Nov. 14, 2026. AP Photo/Brandon Dill

The Nets fell behind by 26 after a Javon Small 3-pointer with 7:08 to play.

"We weren't committed as well on defense, and they played harder than us. That was really it," Day'Ron Sharpe said. "I just felt like we weren't connected, weren't trusting one another, and we've just got to get better at that and we got to keep focused on just staying consistent in our energy."

Randle finished with 22 points but was a minus-18. Sharpe had 16 points and 11 boards. But the Nets allowed 52.9 percent shooting and 42.9 percent from deep.

Brooklyn Nets guard Nolan Traore (10) reacts in the second half of an NBA basketball game against the Memphis Grizzlies in Memphis, Tenn., Saturday, Nov. 14, 2026. AP Photo/Brandon Dill

Memphis' Cedric Coward had a game-high 23 points, while Hendricks added 22 for a Grizzlies team that didn't even have Jerome.

It was a galling way to end the four-game road swing.

"It was things that we can control," Randle said. "But we didn't get enough stops. They made like nine 3s in the first quarter. It's tough when a team gets it going that early. We didn't punch first. We didn't come out with a sense of urgency. And they took advantage of that.

"Frustrating because we want to see our habits translate, and they didn't [Saturday]. So we've got to be better."

#2658. Stats Rundown: 4 numbers to know from the Mavericks’ 127-117 loss at the Cleveland Cavaliers’ JV

The Dallas Mavericks (7-6) turned in a second straight pitiful performance on Saturday, dropping a 127-117 decision to the Cleveland Cavaliers (7-7) at Rocket Arena.Kyrie Irving led all scorers with 34 points on seven made 3-pointers, but no one rode shotgun with him as the Mavericks gave away a winnable game with a putrid second quarter.

Four of the five Cavaliers' regular starters sat with injuries on the second night of a back-to-back set, after travel difficulties related to the temporary ground stop at all U.S. airports beset the team coming back home from its game at the Miami Heat on Thursday. Various injuries were listed on the Cavs' injury report, but the travel difficulties were what really tipped the scales of availability.

Saturday's matchup appeared to offer Cooper Flagg and Kyrie Irving a get-right opportunity after an off night in Thursday's 133-94 loss at the Minnesota Timberwolves. But that's not what happened, of course. Let's see what the numbers tell us.

An unlikely early scoring leader emerged for the Mavericks against the Cavs on Saturday. Caleb Martin paced Dallas with nine points through the first quarter on 4-of-4 shooting, including his only 3-point attempt of the opening frame.

Martin got into the passing lane on a bad pass from Thomas Bryant with 2:25 left in the first, and ran ahead for a dunk to put the Mavs in front, 22-20. He scored his first seven points in the first 4:35 of the game.

But as you may suspect, Martin's emergence as the team's leading scorer early on was not necessarily a harbinger of good things to come for Dallas. After battling to a 33-33 tie at the end of one with an injury-riddled version of the Cavaliers, Dallas started to wobble even more in the second.

The Dallas defense was nonexistent in the second quarter, and things weren't going much better on the offensive end either. The Mavericks surrendered 38 points to a beleaguered Cavaliers team featuring big performances from the likes of Bryant (14 points, six rebounds in first half), rookie second-rounder Meleek Thomas (13 first-half points, 3-of-6 from 3-point range) and Tyrese Proctor (13 and six).

Meanwhile, Flagg and Irving combined to shoot 4-of-18 in the first half, scoring just 14 points between them. That continued a disturbing trend from Thursday's lopsided loss at the Minnesota Timberwolves, when the duo scored just 22 points between them.

The Cavs turned a 33-33 tie after one quarter into a rout by shooting better than 56% from the field in the first half and took a gaudy 71-53 lead into the halftime break.

The Mavericks needed someone to step up in the worst way if they were going to trim the Cleveland lead to somewhere in the neighborhood of 10 points going into the fourth quarter. Enter Irving, finally.

He made 7-of-10 from the field, including 4-of-8 from 3-point land out of halftime as the Mavericks made two separate runs at the Cavs' lead in the third. His third of the third pulled the Mavs to within 95-83 with 2:46 left in the frame. He hit a 28-footer less than a minute later to make it 97-88, giving Irving 17 points in the quarter, but the no-name Cavs had an answer every time.

Mario Hezonja, apparently playing the role of Croatian Kobe Bryant, scored 12 of his own in the third on a pair of made 3-pointers for Cleveland. After the dust settled in a back-and-forth third quarter, the Mavs were still down by 14, 105-91 as the fourth quarter loomed.

What made the frame frustrating is how little the Mavericks' role players did to help Irving out as he single-handedly tried to bring Dallas back. Martin, PJ Washington, Morez Johnson Jr., Zaccharie Risacher and Santi Aldama all combined to score four points on a combined 2-of-7 from the field in the third. Irving scored 20 of his team-high 34 in the third before the Mavericks faded into the Cleveland night down the stretch.

Flagg was nonexistent on both ends of the floor against the Cavs, as he made just six field goals on offense, and got burned time and time again on defense while trying to stay in front of someone named Tyrese Proctor off ball screens. Flagg made just 5-of-12 from the field in limited action on Thursday in the blowout loss at Minnesota.

Proctor has, for most of the early part of the year, been a 20-minute-off-the-bench kind of guy. Against the Mavs on Saturday, he set career-high marks in points, rebounds, and assists on his way to the first triple-double of his career. Proctor burned everyone the Mavs sent at him on Saturday, finishing with 24 points on 10-of-19 shooting, 11 rebounds and 10 assists in the unlikely Cleveland win.

#2656. Lakers vs. Suns Preview: Adjusting without Austin Reaves

The Lakers (11-2) conclude their road trip in Phoenix where they will take on the Suns (5-6) on Sunday. It's the first head-to-head matchup of the season between Pacific Division foes.

The first matchup between the Lakers and Suns will feature two teams coming in with lots of momentum. Los Angeles has won seven straight games while Phoenix caught fire last week by nabbing four of their last five.

The Suns also have their superstar firepower in Devin Booker, who is playing very well as of late and is averaging 25.5. points, 2.5 rebounds and five assists per game this season. His matchup against long-time rival Luka Dončić — who is obviously playing out of this world right now — will take center stage.

Unfortunately, Austin Reaves will not be able to join Dončić since he's recovering from a heel bruise. This then presents another challenge for the Lakers in how to navigate without their second-best player for the time being.

For the Lakers to come away with a win, they'll need to do a few things to keep the Suns in check.

There's no doubt that Luka is the best player on either team in this matchup but the pressure on him increases with Austin out of the lineup. While Dončić will shoulder much of the offensive load, the Lakers' defense will need to step up in containing Booker. That's where Matisse Thybulle, Quentin Grimes and even Colin Sexton come in. The goal is to make sure Booker doesn't get into rhythm the way he has over the last few games.

You'd think that there is no worse rebounding team than the Lakers, but the Suns rank dead last in the league in the category. One reason Phoenix struggles on the boards is its lack of frontcourt size, and that's an area Walker Kessler needs to exploit. The Suns counter by attempting to win the 50-50 balls and forcing turnovers, which the Lakers need to do a better job of.

Note that Phoenix also has the 26th-best defense in the league, so it'll be ideal for the Lakers' offense to overwhelm the Suns right off the bat. Hopefully the Lakers' supporting cast and bench can outplay the likes of Jalen Green, Dillon Brooks, Luke Kennard, among others.

Given their defensive shortcomings, the Suns' best path to winning games is often to simply outshoot their opponents. While it's difficult to account for an unusually hot shooting game, the Lakers' defense must make sure the Suns don't get comfortable and find their rhythm. The Lakers' defense can't be nonexistent in this one.

Hopefully, much like their victory over the Hawks without Reaves, the Lakers can control the pace and dictate the momentum throughout this game. It won't be a walk in the park but the Lakers have shown that they're a team that can overcome obstacles. Let's see if they can do that and extend their winning streak to eight on Sunday.

For the Lakers' injury report, Reaves (left heel bruise) and Cameron Carr (illness) are out.

Bronny James (illness), Adou Thiero (left ankle sprain) and Colin Sexton (right orbital laceration) is questionable.

As for the Suns, Mark Williams (left shoulder surgery) is out.

Approfittando della sosta, a Formello è tempo di programmare il futuro. La dirigenza laziale si muove per consolidare il progetto, convinta dal lavoro di Gattuso dopo un avvio di stagione straordinario che vede attualmente i biancocelesti al primo posto in classifica.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

Stando a quanto rivelato oggi da Il Messaggero, Lotito e Fabiani si sono mossi per blindare Gennaro Gattuso prolungando l'accordo fino al 2029. L'attuale intesa estiva prevede 1,2 milioni di euro con opzione legata al piazzamento fino al 2028. Nonostante le sirene dei top club d'Europa, Gattuso non brama ritocchi personali, concentrandosi piuttosto sui suoi collaboratori: i circa 700 mila euro complessivi suddivisi tra i nove membri dello staff appaiono infatti insufficienti rispetto ai meriti e ai traguardi raggiunti finora.

Prima di firmare il rinnovo a gennaio, il tecnico vuole risposte chiare sul mercato e sulle reali possibilità d'azione della società, che deve prima sistemare i conti in bilancio entro il 30 novembre. Lotito e Fabiani hanno promesso che nessun big partirà a gennaio, neanche di fronte a offerte pazzesche, ma l'allenatore prima di crederci vuole vedere fatti concreti.

#2653. Panthers-Saints game won't have a replay assistant, due to ground stop

The nationwide ground stop that shut down the aviation system has impacted the NFL’s officiating assignments for Sunday games. And while the league has announced the specific changes that will result in non-referees serving as referees for four games on Sunday (with side judge Don Willard working two games in the same day), other adjustments have not been officially announced.

There surely will be others. For now, one game will be shorthanded.

Via Tom Pelissero of Netflix, the Panthers-Saints game won’t have a replay assistant.

Those duties will be handled by the league office. Which will put a strain on the usual resources there, especially in the cluster of 1:00 p.m. ET games. (Panthers-Saints is one of the seven games to be played in that window.)

Given that the league has otherwise adjusted the Week 10 assignments to keep the officials within driving distance of their hometowns, it’s likely that the existing crews will be altered significantly. Which will introduce unfamiliarity and otherwise complicate the effort to get calls right on a consistent basis.

Absent an advance announcement from the league as to the full extent of the changes, they won’t be known until the NFL posts the official Game Books for the Sunday contests.

#2648. Starting with Patriots-Lions, Fox has three windows on Sunday

The last of the early-morning 2026 kickoffs happens today, with the Patriots playing the Lions in Germany. Unlike the others, which were televised by NFL Network, the Week 10 European game will be carried by Fox.

That gives Fox three windows in one day, with the morning game followed by the usual 1:00 p.m. ET window and the every-other-week 4:25 p.m. ET window.

Most of the country will see Vikings-Packers, featuring the return of Kirk Cousins, on Fox at 1:00 p.m. ET. The only Fox game at 4:25 p.m. ET will be 49ers at Cowboys.

With the Fox pregame show starting at 9:00 a.m. ET, it gives Fox more than 10 hours of continuous NFL broadcasting on Sunday. And with five of the six teams having winning records (and the sixth being the Cowboys), the numbers should start large and keep growing — culminating in a very large audience for the late-afternoon window, which has become the biggest of the NFL week.

#2646. Antetokounmpo scores 34, Heat block 14 shots and roll past Pistons 137-117 for 4th straight win

MIAMI — Giannis Antetokounmpo had 34 points, 14 rebounds and eight assists, some of the spectacular variety, and the Miami Heat beat the Detroit Pistons 137-117 on Saturday night for their fourth straight win.

Klay Thompson scored 26 points in his return from a sprained ankle and Bam Adebayo added 20 for the Heat. Davion Mitchell had 15 points and nine rebounds for Miami.

Cade Cunningham had 33 points and eight assists for Detroit, which got 20 points and seven assists from Kevin Huerter.

Miami had nine players record at least one block and finished with 14 as a team — one shy of the franchise record.

The NBA record for players on the same team having at least one block in a game is 10, done twice — both by Golden State, first in 1991 and then again in 2016. The Heat team record for players with at least one block was eight, done on five occasions.

Antetokounmpo finished a weekend where he scored 71 points in a two-day span, after finishing with 37 in Miami's win over Cleveland on Friday night. He also had a through-the-legs assist to Thompson for a 3-pointer in the opening quarter.

It was one of six 3s on the night for Thompson, who is now 26 away from tying former Heat guard Ray Allen (2,973) for the third-most 3-pointers in NBA history.

Miami won for the seventh time in its last nine games and became the fourth team in the last 25 seasons to start 0-4 but rally to a winning record at the 13-game mark. Sacramento (7-6) did it in 2022-23, Oklahoma City (8-5) did it in 2018-19 and Dallas (9-4) did it in 2006-07.

It also matched the best nine-game stretch for the Heat since an 8-1 burst in November 2023.

Pistons: Visit San Antonio on Tuesday night.

#2644. Diving deeper into Cavs 127-117 win over Mavs: Tyrese Proctor leads bench crew to unexpected victory

CLEVELAND — The Cleveland Cavaliers all but punted this game after not getting back from Miami until late this morning. They rested four of the five starters from last night's game (Donovan Mitchell, James Harden, Jarrett Allen, Peyton Watson) rather than risk injury on the second night of a back-to-back. Yet sometimes, the receiving team muffs the punt.

The Dallas Mavericks — who weren't resting their starters — took their eye off the ball. Cleveland took advantage, led by a triple-double from Tyrese Proctor to ruin Kyrie Irving's homecoming and defeat Dallas 127-117.

24 points on 10-of-19 shooting, 11 rebounds, 10 assists, 1 turnover

Proctor has been a revelation over the last week. He backed up an impressive performance in Miami — albeit in a supporting role — with a dominant on-ball showing against the Mavericks.

This was a different outing than what we've seen from Proctor in the past. Instead of being mostly an off-ball shooter, he thrived at creating his own shots. Only one of his 10 field goals was assisted. This included going 5-for-8 on off-the-dribble jumpers.

Scoring wasn't the only thing Proctor provided. He was the primary initiator of the offense, as evidenced by his 10 assists. Some of these led to direct baskets at the rim for Thomas Bryant (19 points and 11 rebounds) out of the pick-and-roll. Overall, six of his assists went to baskets at the rim. He also sprayed the ball to outside shooters and swung the ball on the perimeter, leading to three assists on triples.

Proctor also helped as a defender and rebounder. Kenny Atkinson often talks about how the guards need to be adequate rebounders as well. Proctor was that in a complete all-around performance.

This season, Proctor has been asked to fit into a very specific role. He's done that well, but nights like this show that he's capable of more.

34 points on 11-of-25 shooting, 6 rebounds, 5 assists, 3 steals

Irving's 20 second-quarter points got the Mavs back into this game. He still can be a one-man offense for extended stretches and completely take over games. This was another impressive scoring performance from someone who's had more than his fair share in this building.

22 points on 9-of-12 shooting, 7 rebounds, 4 assists

Hezonja made a strong argument for why he deserves more minutes than he's been getting in recent games. He forced mismatches offensively, and then read how the defense was going to react and consistently made the right play out of it. Hozonja processes the game at such a high level. This elevates the basketball IQ for units he's on the court with.

0 minutes, 0 points, 0 assists, 0 rebounds, 0 steals

Back-to-backs are difficult, especially when travel plans are thrown off as drastically as they were around the country yesterday. It makes sense to err on the side of caution in a situation like this. What's the point of risking an injury for a game that will matter very little in the spring? At the same time, saying that the game should be canceled because of an inconvenience like this is a bad look.

On top of that, the Cavs played some of their most inspiring basketball of the early season on Saturday night without six of the top eight players in their rotation. That is good for the guys who played, but a clear indictment on those who didn't.

Atkinson was asked about rebounding before the game since it's been a consistent issue with the starting group. He gave a long-winded answer that could've been summed up by saying there's only so much coaching can do. "I always tell the coaches, it's 50% on us. It's got to transfer — the message has to get through."

This message, and many others about how they want to play basketball on both ends, is getting through — just not to the guys who will ultimately determine wins and losses in the spring.

13 points, 8 rebounds, 2 assists, 1 steal

Omier made the most of his first real rotation minutes for the Cavs. He was impactful offensively with his ability to finish inside and hit a corner three as well. Defensively, he used his wide frame to play backup five when Bryant wasn't out there.

The Cavs won the minutes Omier played by 11. Getting quality play like this from a two-way big went a long way toward stealing the victory.

Irving received a loud ovation when he was introduced as a starter, and an even louder one when they played a video tribute for his contribution to the 2016 championship team.

"You know, 52 years is a long, long period of time waiting for a championship, and we did it. And I think that's one of the hardest championships — I think. I'm not gonna say it is, I said I think personally it's one of the hardest championships ever in NBA history that we got to accomplish."

The Cavs grabbed 57% of available rebounds (92nd percentile).

The Cavaliers who were available on Saturday showed that they're capable of hearing the message from the coaching staff and applying it on the court.

I wrote about this in yesterday's deep dive from the Miami Heat loss: The Cavs have quietly turned over their supporting cast. Their younger bench players are far more versatile than the specialists we've seen in previous seasons.

The trio of Tyrese Proctor, Meleek Thomas, and Jaylon Tyson have very defined roles when the starters are out there. They've mostly performed well in those situations and have shown glimpses of being able to do more. On Saturday, they proved that they can scale their games up when called upon.

Cleveland needed that trio to be the offensive initiators given who was out, and they did that. The ball was moving quickly around the perimeter, with each being able to attack off the dribble when needed. This resulted in the trio all scoring 18 points or more against a Mavs team actually playing their starters.

This performance on its own doesn't necessarily mean much. It's not uncommon to see NBA teams let up and lose when their opponent is missing half of their rotation. However, this game didn't just come out of the blue; it was a continuation of what we've been seeing pretty consistently for the last week or so — specifically from Proctor and Thomas.

The Cavs are at a weird crossroads. How they've been playing with their star players has led to inconsistent results. We've seen some high highs, but some even lower lows. Something needs to change if they're going to reach the heights they have the potential to.

Surrendering the reins to the young players isn't the answer to their problems. But turning to the style of play that this group has embraced — and the one that all the Cavs did during the 2024-25 season — could be a solution. Just not one we've seen the veterans truly get on board with yet. Maybe this win changes some minds.

#2642. Lazio, Canigiani svela le novità: biglietti del derby e nuovo sponsor tecnico

Il direttore marketing della Lazio fa il punto su derby e Supercoppa e svela a che punto è la scelta dello sponsor tecnico.

Novità importanti sul fronte Lazio, sia per quanto riguarda i biglietti del derby sia per il futuro sponsor tecnico. Marco Canigiani, direttore marketing biancoceleste, ha fatto il punto sulla situazione, soffermandosi anche sulla vendita dei tagliandi per la Supercoppa.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

Sul derby, il dato fornito da Canigiani parla di 16-17mila biglietti già venduti. Considerando anche gli abbonati, i posti occupati si stanno avvicinando a quota 25mila. Dalla prossima settimana, inoltre, la vendita verrà estesa ai possessori delle Fidelity Card.

Novità anche sullo sponsor tecnico. Con Mizuno attualmente in scadenza a fine anno, la Lazio è arrivata al rush finale: sono arrivate diverse offerte e il club ne ha già selezionate un paio. Il marchio giapponese mantiene però un diritto di prelazione.

Secondo quanto riportato da Radiosei, Marco Canigiani ha spiegato nel dettaglio le diverse fasi previste dal club.

Il direttore marketing ha spiegato come si sta sviluppando la prima fase della vendita:

“In questa momento è attiva una fase che abbiamo voluto dedicare agli abbonati della passata stagione, prelazione che non può essere sul posto in cui erano abbonati o nel settore perché magari è stato occupato, ma solo loro possono acquistare in questo momento. Un abbonato può acquistare fino a 4 biglietti, sempre per gli abbonati della scorsa stagione. Dalla prossima settimana la possibilità si amplierà ai possessori delle Fidelity Card, anche loro potranno acquistare fino a 4 biglietti sempre per chi possiede le varie card”.

L'intenzione della Lazio è favorire il più possibile la presenza dei propri sostenitori:

“L’obiettivo ovviamente è preferire la vendita ai nostri tifosi, soprattutto per la Monte Mario; per la Tevere, anche più avanti servirà, la Eagle Card, mentre in Monte Mario partirà la vendita libera, che quindi ci auguriamo sia limitata. La Roma avrà il settore Sud e una iniziale dotazione di Monte Mario sud, poi è chiaro che della vendita libera ne può usufruire chiunque. Le card devono essere retroattive, altrimenti quello che è l’obiettivo poteva essere facilmente aggirabile. Le card hanno un prezzo irrisorio, quindi non sarebbero una barriera. Può acquistare ora chi quindi aveva le card già prima dell’inizio della vendita. Noi al momento abbiamo oltre 16-17mila biglietti. Siamo intorno ai 20mila presenti più gli abbonati, quindi ci avviciniamo ai 25mila posti occupati. Nei Distinti c’è ancora qualche disponibilità”.

Canigiani ha poi sottolineato il potenziale della fase riservata ai possessori delle tessere:

“Potenzialmente i possessori di tessere potrebbero riempiro lo stadio, dipende dalla volontà di farlo; anzi potrebbero anche non bastare i posti. Il biglietto deve essere intestato al possessore delle card nella fase che scatterà lunedì. L’obiettivo è quello di arrivare alla vendita libera con meno posti a disposizione“.

Capitolo Supercoppa: bisognerà attendere le comunicazioni della Lega per conoscere ufficialmente date e modalità di vendita.

“Supercoppa? A breve la Lega comunicherà date e modalità di vendita, anche qui abbiamo previsto diverse fasi. Credo che già la prossima settimana potrà iniziare la vendita. Lo stadio, essendo una gara della Lega, è diviso a metà. Entrambe le card avranno una fase dedicata”.

#2641. Game between Bill Belichick's UNC and Louisville ends in a brawl

But a fight nevertheless happened at the end of the game between Louisville and Bill Belichick’s North Carolina Tar Hells.

The Cardinals led, 16-14, with time ticking away. (UNC had a timeout remaining but hadn’t used it on the final Louisville drive, after a game-sealing interception.) Louisville received the snap and took a knee as the clock hit 15 seconds.

North Carolina, despite not using its final timeout, deployed the Schiano-style effort to blow up victory formation. Which sparked a shoving match match between opposing lineman. Which eventually became a full-blown brawl.

Through it all, time expired and the game ended. It will be interesting to see whether the ACC or the individual schools hand out suspensions as a result of the fracas.

The loss dropped North Carolina to 5-5. The Tar Heels need one win in remaining games against Virginia and NC State to become bowl-eligible in Belichick’s second season on the job.

And that could be harder to do against Virginia next week, if one or more UNC players end up being required to sit out.

#2640. The case for a Domantas Sabonis trade for Utah

The Utah Jazz are in the midst of the worst start in decades. It's an even worse start than the former tanking seasons. Before the season started, the Jazz said they would have a competitive season. And even though the Jazz are close in a lot of these games, they are 1-12 and on an 11-game losing streak. With the Walker Kessler trade behind them, the Jazz are left with a lopsided team in desperate need of starting center play that could support their three young stars: Darryn Peterson, Ace Bailey, and Keyonte George.

That group this season has been elite, hiding behind subpar play from their center and bench. From CraftedNBA.com, here are the Jazz's best players sorted by net rating and showing their best On-Off players.

Utah's trio of Bailey, Peterson, and George is playing winning basketball, and it's an incredible sign for Utah. But outside of those three, it's not looking good. Losing Jaren Jackson Jr. at the beginning of the season has been brutal because his two-way play would have been a huge part of helping Utah get some wins.

Probably the biggest disappointment, though, is Lauri Markkanen's play this season. His off-ball offensive game is high-level as usual, the problem is everything else. He's not producing on the ball, and he has not been a good defender. That's why Utah should consider a potential move for Domantas Sabonis, who wants out of Sacramento. The trade is an easy, player-for-player trade with Lauri Markkanen.

I've thought about this a lot this season, and the more I think about it, the more I like it. Yes, Sabonis has some flaws just like Markkanen does. He's undersized at his position and not a good rim protector. He also struggles in space and on the perimeter defensively, just like Markkanen.

But Sabonis' pros would be huge for this Jazz team and their young COR3, and could provide a skill set that would take them to another level. Yes, Markkanen provides catch-and-shoot threes and cuts to the basket. Utah is getting enough shooting, scoring, and cutting from that young trio. What Utah lacks right now is a starting center. Sabonis would bring what they've been dying for all season, including elite rebounding, screening, passing, and inside scoring. Adding Sabonis would solidify the position in a way that they haven't had all season. Yes, the Jazz can simply wait for Jusuf Nurkic to come back, but with Nurkic's size and his foot injury, it's not a given that he'll stay healthy this season. Also, having Nurkic come back and play 20-25 minutes a night off the bench is best anyway.

Sabonis is also a perfect fit with what Will Hardy does on offense. He can get the ball and run a dribble handoff from the three-point line, then dive, or run simple pick-and-rolls as the screener. With Sabonis setting screens and scoring inside, you can see how Utah's offense could get to an elite level. It's also interesting to think about how well Ace Bailey would fit playing off of him. Sabonis is no Jokic, but he's the next best thing at center, hitting cutters and passing out of the short roll to open shooters. And finally, Sabonis can score inside on a mismatch. If Utah has a mismatch down low, Sabonis can easily take advantage. And when Jaren Jackson Jr. comes back, Sabonis is the perfect fit next to him, with their strengths offsetting each other. Jackson can be the weak-side defender while Sabonis cleans up their rebounding issues.

There's also an elephant in the room for the Jazz right now that needs to be recognized. Lauri Markkanen has simply not lived up to his superstar-level contract. With a move like this, Utah can get off his contract before it becomes untradable. Sabonis' contract is for this season and next, so if we're simply looking at contract relief, it's another bonus for Utah. If Markkanen is also a consistent injury risk and not an elite on-ball scorer over the next three seasons, his contract becomes an albatross with two years after this season and the final year coming in at $53M. Utah can get off that contract sooner rather than later by making this happen. Sabonis' contract runs through this season and next, and then Utah can either extend him or look for another option that fits the timeline of Keyonte George, Darryn Peterson, and Ace Bailey.

For Sacramento, Lauri Markkanen is the perfect fit for Darius Acuff Jr. Acuff can be the hub of everything they do, and Markkanen can do what he does best next to him: take catch-and-shoot threes and score off the ball. Markkanen also provides more spacing for Acuff, which can help him take his game to another level.

Honestly, this one makes a ton of sense for both sides. Most likely, no picks trade sides in this, and Utah can then use their picks from the Kessler trade in other ways, or just simply draft a center prospect for the post-Sabonis era.

#2635. Lions, Jets renegotiated Andre Cisco trade after concerns arose about his physical

A controversy arose after the NFL trade deadline when the Broncos demanded to change the terms of their trade with the Chargers after linebacker Daiyan Henley’s physical. But Henley wasn’t the only traded player whose physical raised concerns.

The Lions also told the Jets they wanted to change the terms of their trade for safety Andre Cisco after concerns about his physical. But unlike the Chargers, the Jets agreed to it, and the Lions ultimately sent the Jets a 2029 sixth-round pick for Cisco after initially agreeing to give up a 2028 sixth-round pick.

Tom Pelissero reports that the modified terms were based on medical concerns. There’s no word on what those concerns were, but Lions coach Dan Campbell said the plan is for Cisco to play on Sunday against the Patriots.

The Jets went along with the Lions’ request, and in the scheme of things the difference between a 2028 sixth-round pick and a 2029 sixth-round pick is minor. Still, it points to an inherent flaw in the NFL’s trade rules: The team acquiring a player has the ability to go back on the trade, or negotiate better terms, after the trade deadline. That puts the team trading the player in a difficult position: After you’ve already told a player you’re trading him, and told another player you’re signing him or bringing him up from the practice squad to take his place, you don’t want to go back on that. So if the team you’re trading with tells you, “We didn’t like his physical, so we’ll back out of the trade unless you take less compensation,” you may feel you have no choice but to accept.

The NFL could resolve that by not allowing trades to be renegotiated after the deadline: Either the player passes the physical and the trade goes through, or the player fails the physical and the trade does not go through. No more half measures like, “We failed him on his physical, but we’ll pass the physical if you agree to take a lesser draft pick for him.”

Another solution could be that physicals for traded players are conducted by an independent, league-appointed doctor, rather than the team’s medical staff. If that doctor says the player passes the physical, the team trading for the player can’t back out.

The Jets and Chargers had different reactions to their trade partners asking to renegotiate the trades, but the situation both teams were faced with highlights potential problems that can arise with the NFL allowing teams to change the terms of trades after the trade deadline.

#2633. ACC Roundup – Three Wins Saturday, But Better Games On Sunday

In Saturday's ACC Action, Georgia Tech survived UNC Asheville, 75-74, Wake Forest handled Southern Utah, 89-51, and Cal knocked off Utah Tech, 79-73.

When we say Georgia Tech survived, that's true-ish. What really happened is a player from Asheville made a brutally foolish mistake.

The Bulldogs hit a three to tie the score at 74-74 with 2.2 seconds left. But then Georgia Tech brought the ball in and Myles Mayfield had an inexplicable moment where he fouled Georgia Tech's Victor Valdes, who followed Scott Cross from Troy to Tech.

Valdes hit one of his free throws to put the game away.

Look at Asheville coach Mike Morrell – he's just devastated. And Mayfield had a pretty good game for the most part, shooting 9-11 for 21 points.

For the Yellow Jackets, Jackson Fields had eight offensive rebounds. We're not sure what the record is in the ACC, but that's pretty damn good.

Tech is undefeated but hasn't played anyone of consequence, really. After Norfolk State, they'll get Georgia in the traditional rivalry game, and we'll get a better sense of what the Yellow Jackets have.

Other than losing to #24 Vanderbilt, Wake Forest hasn't really played anyone either. Southern Utah is not a distinguished program, so it's no surprise that Wake beat them by 38.

What we are paying attention to is that freshman Gavin Placide and sophomore Kevair Kennedy, who transferred from Merrimack, are playing pretty well.

The 6-2 Kennedy finished with 23 points and a highly impressive 10 rebounds. Placide wrapped up with 16 points and seven boards. Twin brother Gallagher had nine points and three rebounds, so the Denver duo called it a night with 25 points and 10 rebounds.

Kennedy is averaging 16.3 points, 5.7 rebounds, and 3.3 assists, while Placide is getting 14.7 points and 7.7 rebounds. Each is also averaging two steals.

Wake Forest will play Mississippi State (coached by Chris Jans, who, along with Wake's Steve Forbes, was an assistant at Wichita State in the Gregg Marshall era), LSU, and UMass in a couple of weeks. We'll see more about this team in that stretch

Cal really struggled to overcome Utah Tech, and fell behind by 11 in the second half. The Bears went up with 1:14 left, but even then, at 74-71, it was no sure thing. Pitt transfer Nojus Indrusaitis converted a three-point play with 0:17 left to make it 77-73, and then Jake Wilkins converted a pair of free throws of his own to make it 79-73.

Not ideal, but a win is better than a loss, obviously.

By the way, what better name could there be for a technical school than Trailblazers?

Three games on Sunday, as Louisville takes on Memphis, BC welcomes New Hampshire to Conte, and we get a game between former Jim Boeheim assistants Gerry McNamara of Syracuse, and Rick Pitino of St. John's.

To put that in perspective, Larry Bird and Magic Johnson were still in school when Pitino was at Syracuse, and when McNamara became his alma mater's head coach, Cameron Boozer had just finished his freshman year at Duke.

Put another way, McNamara was born in 1983, six years before Pitino took the Kentucky job.

They'll play in the Garden, and Pitino has the better team, but given what we've seen so far, we expect Syracuse will give a great effort.

#2632. Observations after Sixers beat Bucks to move to 3-0, Embiid posts triple-double

Observations after Sixers beat Bucks to move to 3-0, Embiid posts triple-double originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia

The Sixers stayed unbeaten Saturday night at Xfinity Mobile Arena, earning a 127-116 win over the Bucks and improving to 3-0 on the season.

Joel Embiid had his 10th career regular-season triple-double, tallying 28 points, 11 rebounds and 10 assists.

On his 30th birthday, Jaylen Brown posted 27 points and five assists. Tyrese Maxey had 26 points. VJ Edgecombe scored 17 and grabbed 13 boards.

The Sixers' absences on the first night of a back-to-back included LeBron James (low back/sciatica management). Sixers head coach Nick Nurse said pregame that he did not know yet who would be available for his team's matchup with the Pistons on Sunday.

Here are observations on the Sixers' victory Saturday:

Dean Wade made his Sixers debut and started in James' place. He'd missed the first two games of the regular season with a left ankle sprain.

The 3-and-D forward scored the night's first points by a sinking a corner three-pointer on the opening possession.

Embiid also had a sharp start. He moved well, made good decisions and served as the main hub of his team's offense in the early going.

The Sixers' seven-time All-Star center has often enjoyed facing Myles Turner. He entered the night with an average of 29.4 points in 18 previous games against the Bucks big man.

Embiid did a little bit of everything in the first quarter, posting eight points, four assists and four rebounds over nine minutes. After snatching an offensive board, Embiid drained a fadeaway jumper to give the Sixers a 10-1 lead.

One of Embiid's assists was quite stylish. He found Edgecombe open beyond the arc with a behind-the-back bounce pass. Edgecombe knocked down the shot and wound up going 3 for 4 from three-point range in the first quarter.

The Sixers added rookie Labaron Philon Jr. to their rotation. Jabari Walker stayed in the mix, though he didn't enter until the 7:36 mark of the second quarter.

Philon played four minutes in his NBA debut and missed his lone shot attempt, a corner three. On defense, Philon allowed a couple of blow-bys off the dribble. He generally looked like he belonged on offense, albeit without any production in his brief run.

Maxey banked in a half-court heave at the first-quarter buzzer to put the Sixers up nine points. The Sixers couldn't carry forward any momentum, however, and began the second quarter poorly.

Adem Bona had another rough stint amid a subpar start to the season. After Anfernee Simons missed a transition layup try, Ryan Rollins' three lifted the Bucks into a 40-37 lead.

The dreadful stretch for the Sixers on both sides of the ball called to mind how they'd fallen into a 29-point deficit Thursday night vs. the Cavaliers before clawing out a comeback win.

The Sixers mustered just seven points in first six minutes of the second quarter and had many stagnant possessions that concluded with contested jumpers. The team's transition defense was dismal for much of the second period. Milwaukee had the game's first 19 fast-break points.

The Sixers regained the lead late in the second quarter. Kentavious Caldwell-Pope made two three-balls in the second and nabbed three first-half steals. Embiid assisted a go-ahead, and-one Walker layup.

Brown hit a three with 11.8 seconds left in the second quarter. Unsurprisingly, his variety of shotmaking skills were useful without James in the lineup.

Even when James or Embiid sit, the Sixers should have a simple advantage in terms of volume of stars over most opponents this year. None of Brown, Embiid or Maxey had the sort of off night that would have improved the Bucks' odds of a road win. They'd all passed the 20-point mark by the end of the third quarter.

Maxey notched another final-possession bucket, this time with a more conventional make. He canned a jumper from the right elbow with 1.7 seconds left in the third to extend the Sixers' lead to 97-87.

The Bucks made a late push in the fourth quarter. Kel'el Ware's put-back, and-one layup cut the Milwaukee's deficit to 117-114.

The Sixers ultimately handled business. Embiid reached his triple-double by assisting a second-chance Brown jumper and and Caldwell-Pope soon drilled a dagger corner three. Embiid even threw down a last-minute dunk for good measure.

For the second consecutive season, the Sixers have a 3-0 start. They got to four wins last year before dropping their first game.

#2631. Arch Manning shakes off 3 interceptions, throws game-winning TD pass as Texas beats LSU

As he has been throughout his college football career, Texas quarterback Arch Manning was a mixed bag on Saturday. But Manning and Texas came out on top.

After throwing three interceptions and seeing his team fall behind LSU 21-10, Manning turned it on late, culminating in a 12-play, 58-yard drive that saw Manning throw the game-winning touchdown pass with three seconds remaining as Texas won 22-21.

“That’s what college football is all about,” Manning said after the game.

Manning’s numbers were not impressive: 19-of-35 for 174 yards and one touchdown with three interceptions and four sacks, plus 35 yards and a touchdown running. But when Texas needed him to march the offense down the field at the end of the game, he did it. His touchdown pass to Raleek Brown was a perfectly placed ball, and he also ran for two first downs on the game-winning drive.

For No. 6 Texas, the win means they’ll almost certainly be in the College Football Playoff, as they’ll be heavy favorites the next two weeks against Arkansas and Texas A&M. For LSU, the loss knocks first-year coach Lane Kiffin out of playoff contention.

Manning, the scion of the first family of quarterbacks, will have an opportunity do what neither his grandfather Archie nor his uncles Peyton and Eli ever did: Win a national championship.

#2630. 49ers will fly to Colorado tonight to begin acclimating to altitude for Mexico City game

The 49ers won’t fly home after today’s game in Dallas. Instead, they’ll immediately begin preparation for next Sunday night’s game in Mexico City.

The team plane will fly to Colorado Springs tonight, as coach Kyle Shanahan believes spending a week at altitude will help the 49ers’ chances against the Vikings next week at Estadio Azteca, the highest stadium the NFL ever plays in.

“I think it helps,” Shanahan said. “I grew up mainly in Denver, and I know how bad it would be for me. No matter how good of shape you’re in, you come home from college and you run up the stairs and you’re out of breath. It takes some time to get used to altitude. I know when you go to play in Denver it’s always a challenge, and Mexico City is higher than Denver. It’s not make or break, but I do think it makes you a couple percent better.”

Shanahan thanked Air Force head coach Troy Calhoun for allowing the 49ers to use his team’s practice facility in Colorado Springs, as he did before the 49ers’ Mexico City game in 2022. Air Force’s Falcon Stadium is at 6,621 feet. Estadio Azteca has an altitude of 7,280 feet — exactly 2,000 feet higher than Denver’s Mile High elevation.

Next Sunday night will be the 49ers’ second international game of the season. They opened the season in Australia, where their decision to arrive a week early to get used to the time difference was credited as one of the reasons for their impressive performance against the Rams. Now they hope another weeklong preparation will yield similar results.

#2629. Paul George flips the script — and the bird — in Philadelphia return

Paul George flips the script — and the bird — in Philadelphia return originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia

PG-13 was rated R in his return to Philadelphia.

The middle finger Paul George directed toward one baseline fan only reinforced that rating.

Tuesday night was expected to revolve around Jaylen Brown and Jayson Tatum sharing an NBA court as opponents for the first time. Instead, the other headliner in the summer's blockbuster trade stole the show.

George scored a game-high 36 points in Boston's 123-101 win over the Sixers. He shot 14 for 22 from the floor, made six of his 11 three-point attempts and scored 14 consecutive Boston points in the fourth quarter.

The game was tied at 79 with 3:19 remaining in the third quarter. Boston outscored Philadelphia 44-22 from that point forward.

The Celtics went nine minutes and 20 seconds without making a two-point field goal during the second half. Instead, they made nine consecutive field goals from three, the second-longest such streak by a Sixers opponent over the last 30 seasons.

Payton Pritchard opened the fourth with consecutive threes. George followed with eight straight points, helping the Celtics begin the quarter on a 14-0 run that turned a competitive game into a rout.

George's return carried a complicated history. His two seasons with the Sixers were repeatedly interrupted by injuries, but he also played a significant role in their most memorable playoff run in years.

Last spring, George helped the Sixers overcome a 3-1 deficit to eliminate Boston in seven games. He averaged 17.4 points and shot 55 percent from three during the series.

Tyrese Maxey was happy to see his former teammate Tuesday, even if he disliked what followed.

"It was good to see Paul," Maxey said. "I love him, love his family. … He gave us everything he had while he was here. We know what he did in the playoffs last year. Great person, great family, and we'll see him again."

Maxey then added one important qualifier.

George instead scored from nearly everywhere.

"He had some open threes. He had some pull-up threes. He had some middies," Maxey said. "He played within the game, too. That's what Paul does. He plays within the game. He takes what the defense gives him, and we gave him too many open looks tonight.

"PG, we know what PG does. We shouldn't even be allowing him to get up 11 threes, and that's on us."

Nick Nurse watched George attack the Sixers in several ways.

"He really had it going," Nurse said. "He'd post up, and-one, fallaways. He went down the lane, high archer off the glass, and-one. He scored in about every way he could tonight."

George heard boos during his return and said the arena carried the atmosphere, though not quite the intensity, of a playoff game.

"This building can be very electric as well," George said. "It was fun. It was fun to play in this environment."

One interaction extended beyond the usual reception for a returning player.

During a stoppage, the ball rolled toward a fan seated along the baseline. George said the fan looked directly at him before dropping the ball instead of returning it.

"There was a fan being an a–," George said. "The ball rolled to him. He looked me dead in my eyes, dropped the ball on the ground as if I'm a dog to go fetch or go get it, instead of passing the ball to me like a normal fan would do.

"And so, yeah, then I rolled him a middle finger in return."

#2626. With trade offers rejected, Titans' plans for Tony Pollard come into question

All the factors had lined up for a Tony Pollard trade. With a trade not happening, the Titans’ future plans for Pollard come into question.

At 1-7, the Titans aren’t contenders. Pollard is in the final year of his contract. While a compensatory draft pick becomes possible in 2028 (depending on Tennessee’s 2027 free-agent acquisitions and losses), the Titans could have gotten a draft pick in 2027 if they’d traded him.

What could they have gotten? As we hear it, they turned down a fourth-round pick and a player. (The Packers and the Broncos were the two teams linked to Pollard.)

So what’s the plan for Pollard? Maybe they want to keep Pollard beyond 2026. He’s in the last season of a three-year, $21.75 million deal. He’s making $7.25 million this year.

And Pollard is on track for his fifth straight 1,000-yard season. He’s not even in the top 20 highest-paid running backs by annual average. The franchise tag at the position for 2027 is expected to be in the range of $15 million.

Pollard will be 30 in April. That makes it harder to put a proper number on his next contract. But if the Titans weren’t willing to take the best offer they could get for him, it suggests that they have a plan premised on potentially signing him to a new contract.

The decision to keep Pollard could be as simple as the Titans not being confident in their alternatives. Pollard has 147 touches in eight games. His backup, Tajae Spears, has 33 in six games. Rookie Nick Singleton has seven in four games. Julius Chestnut has no touches in eight games.

The answer could be that simple. The Titans had insufficient confidence in their other options if Pollard was traded. Which would have complicated the ongoing effort to develop quarterback Cam Ward.

Regardless, the Titans had a chance to get something now (we don’t know the name of the player that was offered; it could have been a running back) and a 2027 draft pick by trading Pollard. They decided not to.

Pollard will now keep going, and quite possibly finish with more than 1,000 yards again. Which could result in Pollard leaving in 2027 — possibly with the Titans not getting a compensatory draft pick in 2028.
