#2625. Barlow ‘making progress,' Embiid out vs. Pacers, more on Sixers

Barlow 'making progress,' Embiid out vs. Pacers, more on Sixers originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia

Dominick Barlow decided to finish his post-practice workout Saturday with a windmill dunk.

While Barlow remains out with a "lower back stress reaction" listing on the Sixers' injury report, it's one sign that he's trending up in his rehab process.

"He's making progress," Sixers head coach Nick Nurse said. "He was a part of the practice today. It's kind of a game day type of practice … so it wasn't super intense, as you might expect. But he was out there doing some stuff. He's progressing. Just don't know when he'll be ready to go, but at least he's making some progress now."

Barlow was one of the Sixers' top role players last season, starting 59 games and contributing in a variety of areas. He averaged 7.7 points, 4.8 rebounds, 1.2 assists and 0.9 steals in 23.8 minutes per game.

"Size, athleticism, rebounding," Dean Wade said of the fifth-year forward. "He's another guy that can switch one through five."

Whenever the 6-foot-9 Barlow is available for his season debut, the Sixers will welcome him back as another option at center.

With Ariel Hukporti's preseason Achilles tendon tear and Adem Bona's cervical spine sprain, the team is light on healthy resources at the five. And Joel Embiid (right foot plantar fascia injury management) will sit Sunday afternoon vs. the Pacers on the first leg of a back-to-back. He'll presumably return to the lineup when the Sixers visit the Nets on Monday night.

"I think (Barlow) is probably going to have to play more five than we envisioned," Nurse said, "but Jabari (Walker) is doing that as well. If the situation calls for that, I imagine that's where he'll help the most."

With the Delaware Blue Coats hosting the Maine Red Claws on Friday and Saturday, the Sixers saw an opportunity for two players outside of the regular rotation to log minutes with their G League affiliate.

Rookie guard Labaron Philon Jr. suited up Friday and third-year wing Justin Edwards played both games. Philon posted 20 points, nine rebounds and eight assists in a blowout loss. Edwards shot just 1 for 10 from the floor in the first game, but he scored 23 points on 9-for-17 shooting in Saturday's win.

Nurse has largely kept a tight rotation early in the season and the 10-3 Sixers haven't had many lopsided games with ample garbage time. As of Saturday night, the Sixers ranked 29th in the NBA in bench minutes per game.

"My first belief is it's hard to get better unless you're playing," Nurse said. "That kind of trumps everything, in my opinion. Just historically, we've had a number of guys that have gone down to those games, respected it … and it's really helped them in their careers. … It's been a minute for these guys — both of them — since they've had any real court time.

"So that fit into the schedule well. … I think it will also help them to just find some rhythm, find their legs a little bit. We're going to need everybody at some point, so keep 'em going."

VJ Edgecombe was among the crowd Friday night at Chase Fieldhouse.

"They're my brothers, man," he said. "Labaron, Justin, (Caleb Love), (Rayan Rupert). I just wanted to show love. … I didn't have (anything) to do yesterday. … We have that relationship off the court, too. I'm just being supportive and showing them that I care about them."

More: Are the Columbus Blue Jackets' playoff hopes already teetering?

Bowness, 71, is scheduled to undergo further testing Nov. 16 that will prevent him from traveling with the team to open a four-game road trip. General manager Don Waddell said Bowness is considered "day-to-day" until more is known about something that began ailing him prior to a Nov. 12 morning skate.

He's just got some things that are affecting him that we need to figure out ... the doctors need to figure out."

Granato, former head coach of the Buffalo Sabres, ran the bench against the Lightning and Flyers with assistants Trent Vogelhuber, Jared Boll and goaltending coach Niklas Backstrom handling their usual roles. #2621. Four things to watch as Sixers look to respond against Raptors

Four things to watch as Sixers look to respond against Raptors originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia

The Sixers will not need to wait long for an opportunity to move past their most lopsided loss of the season.

Less than 48 hours after Boston's 123-101 win exposed several of Philadelphia's early weaknesses, the Sixers will host the Toronto Raptors on Thursday night at Xfinity Mobile Arena.

The Raptors are coming off a difficult meeting with the Celtics, too. Toronto led Boston by 22 points Wednesday before being outscored 61-34 over the final 29:24 of a 98-93 loss.

Philadelphia enters at 9-3 following Tuesday's defeat. Toronto is 5-6 and will complete a back-to-back and its third game in four nights.

LeBron James has been ruled out because of low-back and sciatica management. Joel Embiid is questionable with right plantar fascia injury management. Toronto will be without Kawhi Leonard, Scottie Barnes and Nate Bittle.

Here are four areas to watch as the Sixers try to respond.

Few teams have forced opponents into mistakes as frequently as Toronto.

The Raptors have generated 18.9 turnovers per game, the highest mark in the NBA. They are also averaging 10.9 steals and nearly 15 offensive rebounds.

The Sixers have countered that type of pressure well. Their 13.0 turnovers per game are tied for one of the lowest marks in the league.

Toronto's length remains disruptive even without Leonard and Barnes. The Raptors regularly crowd ball handlers, reach into passing lanes and send multiple players toward the offensive glass. Jakob Poeltl supplies size inside while RJ Barrett, Ja'Kobe Walter and Collin Murray-Boyles can create problems away from the ball.

The Raptors' pressure can punish a careless pass twice. It takes away a Sixers possession and gives Toronto an opportunity to score before the defense gets organized.

Philadelphia has largely avoided those mistakes while adjusting to a new lineup and playing at a quicker pace. Maintaining that control without James, who has handled a significant share of the playmaking, will be one of Thursday's clearest challenges.

Toronto has not built its offense around half-court shooting.

The Raptors are averaging 49.6 paint points and 16.4 fast-break points. Even while shorthanded Wednesday, they scored 18 points in transition against Boston.

That presents a direct test for a Sixers defense allowing 16.5 fast-break points per game, the fourth-highest figure in the NBA. Philadelphia has also surrendered 49.5 paint points per contest.

The first concern will be slowing the ball.

Immanuel Quickley returned Wednesday after missing two games with right hamstring soreness. He gives Toronto another guard capable of attacking early in the shot clock, while Barrett has consistently looked to get downhill with Leonard and Barnes unavailable.

Poeltl can create scoring chances without having a play called for him. He runs the floor, screens for Toronto's guards, rolls toward the rim and cleans up misses.

The Sixers have been effective in transition themselves, averaging 17.1 fast-break points. Maxey and VJ Edgecombe can change ends quickly after a stop, but Philadelphia must secure the ball first.

Thursday's game could swing on which team gets to run and which one is forced to create against a set defense.

Toronto provided an extreme example Wednesday of how quickly the three-point line can alter a game.

The Raptors entered their matchup against Boston shooting 31.8 percent from beyond the arc. They proceeded to hit 10 of their 18 attempts in the first quarter, tying a franchise record for threes in a period.

They went 6 for 25 over the final three quarters.

After Wednesday, Toronto is shooting 32.4 percent from three this season. The Sixers should not treat the Raptors like an elite perimeter team. They also cannot allow them to find early confidence through uncovered catch-and-shoot attempts.

Walter made five threes Wednesday and scored a team-high 17 points. Rookie Allen Graves added 13 points, while Quickley, Barrett and Jamison Battle are all willing shooters when the ball reaches them in rhythm.

Philadelphia's problems against Boston extended beyond the Celtics making difficult shots. The Sixers were late on several closeouts and occasionally allowed too much separation while navigating screens.

Toronto does not rely on the three as heavily as Boston. Wednesday showed it can still build a lead quickly when those shots start falling.

The Raptors expended significant energy Wednesday before traveling to Philadelphia.

They scored 38 first-quarter points, built a 22-point lead and then watched Boston erase the entire margin before the end of the third quarter. Quickley and Barrett each played more than 31 minutes. Poeltl and Walter both played at least 29.

The Sixers should have the fresher legs. Whether they take advantage could become apparent early.

Philadelphia has averaged 26.3 first-quarter points with a minus-2.2 scoring margin in opening periods. Slow starts have forced the Sixers to play from behind several times, including in their 29-point comeback against Cleveland.

An aggressive start would make Toronto respond quickly after a draining loss. Maxey and Edgecombe can apply pressure by pushing the ball after defensive rebounds instead of allowing the Raptors to set their pressure defense.

James' absence will require an adjustment. Maxey, Brown and Anfernee Simons should handle more of the ball and more of the decisions that come with initiating the offense.

If Embiid plays, the Sixers can make Toronto work through Poeltl by establishing him inside. If Embiid sits, Philadelphia's size concerns will become more pronounced with Adem Bona, Dominick Barlow and Ariel Hukporti also unavailable.

The Sixers have a rest advantage against a depleted opponent coming off an emotional loss. Their response should begin well before the fourth quarter.

#2619. Bills Mafia’s confidence reaches season high ahead of Week 10 at Jets

If you've been a part of Buffalo Rumblings for a bit now, you're likely familiar with our weekly Reacts polls. Well, once again, we asked your thoughts about the Buffalo Bills and you reacted!

Things are pretty darn good in Bills Country these days, thanks to Buffalo's 7-1 record and current place atop the list in the AFC playoff list. There are a lot of games left to play, but if the season ended today, the Bills would have earned the number-one seed and a bye week to begin the playoffs. Remember, all this is happening while the team navigates a first-time head coach in Joe Brady, and a first-time NFL defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard.

Buffalo's offense is legit, ranking first in the NFL in points per game (32.0) and also No. 1 in total yards per game (386.4). As for the defense, it's appears to be turning the right corners, improving to a middle-of-the-pack unit overall since the bye week. That's after spending a bulk of the early season among the worst defenses in the league.

Quarterback Josh Allen and running back James Cook III have once again put the NFL on notice, which is of course due in no small measure to the team's offensive line and a bevy of skill players who are equally interested in blocking defenders into tomorrow on any snap.

Is 7-1 a surprise? Likely not given Allen. Yet it's still worth wondering how much leeway Brady and the new coaching staff should get in their first season, even considering Allen. It's worth noting Buffalo's recent favorable stretch of games against backup and emergency quarterbacks. That shouldn't excuse away their legitimacy as a Super Bowl contender. Good teams defeat bad teams, and the Bills have done that without little problem.

Impressively, Buffalo is the only undefeated road team (4-0) left in the NFL this season. Winning is tough in general, but doing so on the road presents teams with the final boss of football challenges.

If our latest poll results are any indication, confidence is contagious. Bills Mafia has bought in — no strings attached. Heading into Buffalo's Week 10, 95% of Rumblings voters are confident in the current direction of the team under Brady, Leonhard, and president of football operations/general manager.

You may be curious to see what fan confidence numbers look like up to this point in the season, which, if true, means you're in luck. Now before I proceed, I want to provide a massive disclaimer about the data in this next graphic. This one image was generated for us by the kind folks at SB Nation, and they used ChatGPT to create it.

As someone who makes a living as a writer and photographer, I loathe AI and what its creation and mostly unnecessary existence could mean for my professional future. I don't enjoy that this graphic was made with AI, and I will continue doing all I can to combat its use where I have sway. Every word, letter, and character you so generously grant my writing is 100% authentically me — and I intend to keep it that way.

That said, when a very kind request is asked of me from team leadership that I admire and respect, I'm happy to oblige. In the past, I've simply generated similar season-long graphics in Excel or Photoshop without AI. Perhaps readers don't believe this is something I should spend so many words (and in the wee hours between night and day) on — that AI is inevitable.

Well, for at least this next image it is:

So, what can we take away here from that which has begun taking from humans? It's hardly Earth-shattering, but like almost every team's fan base, the beginning of the season is filled with massive (where are my Rumblers playing drinking games to this word?) expectations. That usually sets an often-difficult-to-maintain high bar.

Yet lo and behold, we have a new season high this week. Winning, so contagious.

That low mark? You know what that's all about… those pesky New England Patriots, and Buffalo's only loss so far this season.

Can the Bills maintain their current level of play? Honestly, it still feels like they have quite a bit to go before reaching their full potential. However, big games await within the pressure cooker that is winter football. That's precisely why Beane went all out as able at the trade deadline. Buffalo can leave nothing to chance, regardless of encouraging signs on defense.

Speaking of Beane and the team's front office, let's tackle the results for our other poll question…

The ever-scrutinized Beane once again made a trade-deadline move to bring in a talented veteran player. While many thought the Bills would struggle to swing too big due to salary cap concerns. Some were resigned to the idea of Beane doing nothing before the deadline came and went, only to be pleasantly surprised.

I'm of course talking about safety Amani Hooker, who joins the Bills as the current interception co-leader. Buffalo prioritized a need at safety following C.J. Gardner-Johnson's release, and Damar Hamlin's subsequent promotion to starting safety. Where CJGJ looked out of sorts, Hamlin settled things and played competent football.

But to potentially add someone of Hooker's talent was a situation Beane refused to ignore. It eventually worked out in his favor after lunch the day of the trade deadline, with Buffalo sending a 2027 second-round pick to the Tennessee Titans to land Hooker and a 2027 fifth-round pick in return.

We asked Rumblers what they thought of the trade — a move that provides the Bills with a new starting safety under contract for the next two seasons. As you can imagine, the trade was met with rave reviews.

Leading the way were 71% of voters who gave Beane and Buffalo an "A" for the trade. That was followed by 28% of voters more comfortable stamping a "B" on the trade in the early hours. You can likely ignore the 1% of voters who gave the trade an "F".

The great news is that Hooker is expected to make his Bills debut this afternoon in New Jersey against the Jets.

Are you curious to see how Jets fans over at Gang Green Nation feel about their team heading into Week 10? Wonder no more: Just 29% of voters at GGN are confident right now in this year's Jets team.

#2617. Observations after Sixers lose 1st Brown vs. Tatum matchup, George scores 36

Observations after Sixers lose 1st Brown vs. Tatum matchup, George scores 36 originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia

Round 1 of the new-look Sixers vs. the new-look Celtics decisively went Boston's way on Tuesday night.

In the first meeting between the teams since the July trade that sent Jaylen Brown to Philadelphia and Paul George to Boston, the Celtics earned a 123-101 win at Xfinity Mobile Arena.

The Sixers dropped to 9-3 and the Celtics improved to 9-2.

George was the game's brightest star, scoring 36 points on 14-for-22 shooting. Jayson Tatum added 21 points.

Tyrese Maxey's 24 points led the Sixers. Brown was hampered by foul trouble in his heavily anticipated first outing against Tatum. He posted 13 points, five rebounds and two assists in 26 minutes.

The Sixers will host the Raptors on Thursday night. Here are observations on their blowout loss to the Celtics:

To no one's surprise, Brown and Tatum guarded each other to open the night.

VJ Edgecombe defended a former teammate in George, who scored Boston's first four points with a pair of pure jumpers. On the other end, Maxey made the Sixers' first three field goals.

Judging by volume, the home fans cared most about the much-scrutinized Brown vs. Tatum matchup. The crowd was excited early when Brown snagged a steal and then dished to Maxey for a fast-break three-pointer. The fans also dialed up the noise when Brown sized up Tatum in isolation. He wound up dribbling the ball off his foot and out of bounds. Tatum pointed to signal it was Celtics ball.

Boston's star forward had a productive first quarter, posting 11 points. He scored an easy two when he used a back screen to break free from Brown and convert a layup that put the Celtics up 11-7. Boston began 9 for 12 from the floor as a team.

As for Brown, he sat shortly after being called for his second foul with 6:48 left in the first quarter.

Brown re-entered at the start of the second quarter. The Sixers still struggled to eat into Boston's lead.

A Sam Hauser triple extended the Celtics' advantage to 12 points. There was some audible frustration in the building after Brown missed two free throws on the next possesion.

The Sixers' deficit hit 16 points on a Hugo Gonzalez jumper. Meanwhile, the Sixers missed 12 of their first 14 three-point tries. While some of those shots were open looks that simply didn't go down, the Sixers also rushed up several contested jumpers before they made Boston's defense do serious work.

In the bigger picture, it wouldn't be remotely surprising if shooting stands out as a weak area for the Sixers come the trade deadline. They entered the game ranked 27th in the NBA in three-point frequency outside of garbage time and 22nd in three-point accuracy, according to Cleaning the Glass.

Joel Embiid (16 points, six rebounds) had an injury scare late in the second quarter when he fell hard after missing a layup in transition. He rose gingerly and limped through the final 30 seconds or so of the first half.

The Sixers' star big man was fine to start the third quarter and even drained a long-overdue three on the opening possession. He'd been in a terrible outside shooting slump (3 for 32 from deep on the season) before that shot.

Brown's foul trouble persisted. He picked up his fourth personal with 10:40 to go in the third quarter.

The Sixers stormed back without him and their defense played a large role. After LeBron James rumbled in for a layup, Dean Wade stonewalled Payton Pritchard on the perimeter to force a shot-clock violation. Wade later canned a three to even the contest at 76-all.

The Celtics responded and Tatum led the charge. His third-quarter exploits included a highlight slam on James and a top-of-the-key three to build Boston's lead back up to nine points.

Pritchard buried a three on the first possession of the fourth quarter and the Celtics' advantage kept growing. George celebrated a triple that stretched his team's lead to 100-82. The Sixers' spirits were considerably lower as they headed to their bench for a timeout. As a Sixer, George only had one higher-scoring game (39 points) than his performance Tuesday.

George and Tatum were each excellent in Philadelphia. Outside of Maxey, who finished 8 for 12 from the field, the Sixers didn't receive similar games from their stars.

Brown will be back in Boston on Jan. 21 when the Sixers visit the Celtics. He'll try to even the score.

#2616. Demarvion Overshown wasn't fined for running onto field in street clothes

In the fourth quarter of a Week 9 game the Cowboys led by only three points, Dallas forced — and recovered — a fumble by Colts running back Jonathan Taylor. The ensuing celebration drew a penalty.

Said referee Clay Martin in announcing the specific of theinfraction, “Unsportsmanlike conduct by Dallas, who had a non-uniformed player in the blue sweats and a stocking cap come onto the field to celebrate.”

The non-uniformed player in the blue sweats and the stocking cap was linebacker DeMarvion Overshown, who was inactive for the game due to injury.

While violations of the celebration rules routinely spark fines, Overshown was not financially penalized by the league.

It’s possible Overshown got some sort of punishment from the team, especially since owner and G.M. Jerry Jones rejected Overshown’s claim that he didn’t know it was against the rules for a player not in uniform to run onto the field for a celebration.

“I don’t think that,” Jones said. “I really don’t. I think that he’s been involved in football at Texas, and he’s been involved here, and he knows that, at every level, a nonparticipant can’t run out on the field.”

Every player should have known the rule before last Sunday. Given what happened in the Dallas game, where the lost 15 yards of field position set the stage for a game-tying field goal by the Colts (the Cowboys eventually won, 27-23), there’s even less of an excuse to not know it now.

#2615. Falcons vs. Chiefs: What will Week 10’s win or loss mean for Atlanta?

The Falcons cap off a very eventful week which saw them trade away major contributors on both offense and defense in Jessie Bates III and Ryan Neuzil, with a meeting against the team that built the dynasty of the modern NFL in the Kansas City Chiefs.

Atlanta is currently in a unique situation, sitting in between playoff contention due to their pathetic division and a top 10 pick, and their decision to ship out contributors indicates that they have no delusions on the present as one eye firmly stays looking toward the future.

With the bye week ahead, the Birds have an opportunity to really lock in on having the best of both worlds with a victory, and possibly a more gleaming future with continued losses. It's a rare scenario where the perspective can be that of glass half full either way.

Here is the scenario the Falcons face if they beat the Kansas City Chiefs in Week 10, as well as if they lose.

They'll stamp in another victory against an opponent they were wholly unlikely to defeat, as their resume will have very impressive victories over the Packers, 49ers and now Chiefs up until this point. Their continued identity of showing up against the good teams will be solidified.

It's hard to believe, sitting here at 3-6 and in the basement of the NFC South, but the Falcons would put themselves in a decent position in their division going into the bye week. With Tampa on a bye, Atlanta would move ahead of them and they would jump the loser of the Saints – Panthers matchup this weekend to control sole possession of second place, just 0.5 games back of first.

The odds won't shift much in either direction for Atlanta as far as the playoffs are concerned, according to playoffstatus.com. They currently sit at 17%, a win would increase that to 21% regardless of other outcomes around the NFL.

The Falcons would break a three game losing streak at the hands of the Chiefs, earning their first victory in this matchup since 2012.

They would go into the bye week likely with an even greater eye toward the future. I would predict that coming out on the other side we would see the likes of Aveion Terrell, Billy Bowman and other young pieces be given more of an opportunity over veterans.

They would remain in play in the division no matter what, sitting at 1.5 games back of either the Saints or the Panthers. If Panthers are victorious and if they win their matchup again next week while Atlanta is on the bye, the Birds would find themselves at a full 2.0 games back with no tiebreaker essentially needing to make up three full games in the second half of the season. With games against the Lions and Vikings on the other side, the playoff dream is likely to be slipping quickly.

The playoff odds would decrease from 17% to a meager 13% and then even lower than that depending on what happens next week during the bye.

As unlikely as it may be, a Cardinals victory against the Rams would see Atlanta's pick at minimum reach as high as 8th at the end of this week.

#2613. Observations after Sixers shake off slow start, Embiid injury scare to win

Observations after Sixers shake off slow start, Embiid injury scare to win originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia

The Sixers brushed off their blowout loss to the Celtics and got back in the win column Thursday night.

They overcame a first-quarter deficit as high as 17 points and earned a 123-112 home win over the Raptors. The Sixers moved to 10-3 and Toronto fell to 5-7.

Tyrese Maxey had 27 points and eight assists. Joel Embiid added 20 points.

Jaylen Brown tallied 18 points and six rebounds. VJ Edgecombe posted 15 points, eight rebounds and a season-high eight assists. Anfernee Simons scored 17 points and shot 5 for 6 from three-point range.

RJ Barrett recorded 31 points and 14 rebounds. Immanuel Quickley had 26 points and six assists.

The Sixers were without LeBron James (low back/sciatica management), Adem Bona (cervical spine sprain), Dominick Barlow (lower back stress reaction) and Ariel Hukporti (right Achilles tendon tear).

The team told reporters Thursday morning that Bona will be re-evaluated in approximately one week and that Barlow participated in shootaround. The 23-year-old forward also went through a pregame workout on the Xfinity Mobile Arena floor. There's no formal timetable for his return.

Toronto's sidelined players included Kawhi Leonard and Scottie Barnes.

The Sixers will face the Pacers on Sunday afternoon in Philadelphia. Here are observations on their victory over the Raptors:

Dean Wade began the game in James' normal spot. The Sixers started slowly, missing their first foul field goals and opening 1 for 8 from three-point range.

He stayed down after setting a ball screen and having an apparent knee-to-knee collision with Ja'Kobe Walter. The Sixers called timeout with 8:30 left in the first quarter and Embiid grabbed at his right knee. He eventually rose with assistance from teammates and Sixers head athletic trainer Kevin Johnson, then limped back to the locker room. Jabari Walker entered.

At the 5:26 mark of the first quarter, Embiid checked back in to cheers from the home fans.

"I knew that he didn't twist it or anything," Maxey said. "I knew it was a knee-to-knee, so I wasn't too worried. He kept saying, 'I just got kneed.' That still hurts, though."

Embiid ended up logging 28 minutes, though he certainly wanted to play more.

"He was very, very motivated to play," Sixers head coach Nick Nurse said. "It was hard to get him out for his scheduled rests tonight, which is a good problem sometimes."

While Embiid's return was a major positive development, the Sixers fell further behind. The Raptors' lead swelled to 32-16 with a Jamison Battle three-pointer and Nurse burned a timeout.

Simons sunk a buzzer-beating three to conclude the first quarter, cutting the Sixers' deficit to nine points.

"Those are big momentum plays that usually have some weight to them and carry you into the next moment," Nurse said.

The Sixers kept rolling against a shorthanded Toronto team playing on the second night of a back-to-back. Simons nailed a triple to kick off the scoring in the second quarter. Brown buried a mid-range jumper and Edgecombe jammed in a crowd-pleasing dunk to give the Sixers a 35-34 edge.

Brown and Edgecombe shined in the second quarter both as individuals and as a duo. The Sixers need Edgecombe to attack a bit more offensively when he shares the floor with Brown and bench players. It doesn't hurt for the second-year guard to have that clarity about his role in those units.

"He's one of our better playmakers," Maxey said of Edgecombe. "He's really good at getting downhill and creating for himself and others."

The Sixers' only three bench rotation players were Walker, Simons and Kentavious Caldwell-Pope (11 points, five assists). In addition to Walker, Wade got center minutes behind Embiid.

Embiid picked up his third foul with 2:23 left in the second quarter and had to take a seat. The teams were tied at 60 apiece through two periods.

The game remained even for much of the third, but Maxey fueled an 11-0 Sixers run late in the quarter.

His speed and the Sixers' collective focus on pushing the pace whenever possible allowed the team to get regular points before Toronto could set its defense. Maxey zoomed in for a layup, then tossed the ball ahead to Brown for an easy bucket. Brown assisted a Simons three. Walker converted a fast-break lay-in and canned a three on the first possession of the fourth quarter. All of a sudden, the Sixers held a 101-87 lead.

Brown, Edgecombe and the bench gave the Sixers more good minutes early in the fourth quarter. They sealed the deal without any late drama. And the fans chanting for a Tacko Fall appearance got their wish with a final-minute entrance by the 7-foot-6 center.

#2609. ‘Hard to win': Simons, Walker carry Portland lessons into Sixers roles

'Hard to win': Simons, Walker carry Portland lessons into Sixers roles originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia

Anfernee Simons and Jabari Walker shared the floor for 128 games in Portland. The Trail Blazers won 43 of them.

They sat beside one another in the Sixers' interview room Thursday night after a victory and discussed what the other 85 taught them.

"Whether you've got a big role or a small role, it's hard to win in the NBA," Simons said. "We've seen it firsthand."

Their roles were considerably different then.

Simons was an established starter entrusted with creating and scoring. Walker, a 2022 second-round pick, was trying to establish himself in a rotation. During their three overlapping seasons, Portland went 33-49, 21-61 and 36-46. The Blazers missed the playoffs each year.

Both are now reserves on a Sixers team constructed to contend. In nine games they've both appeared in this season, Philadelphia is 7-2.

They provided 26 points, 11 rebounds and six three-pointers in the Sixers' 123-112 win over the Raptors at Xfinity Mobile Arena. Simons scored 17 points and shot 5 for 6 from three-point range. Walker recorded nine points and eight rebounds, including four on the offensive glass.

The Sixers outscored Toronto by 24 points during Simons' 23 minutes. Neither former Blazer committed a turnover.

Their production helped Philadelphia overcome a 17-point first-quarter deficit and improve to 10-3 without LeBron James.

"You learn once you come off the bench to kind of read the game before you get in there," Simons said. "Obviously, we started off kind of slow. You just want to go in, bring some energy, get some stops, get out and run. I think everybody who got off the bench brought energy."

Simons supplied an immediate lift with a deep three-pointer at the first-quarter buzzer. His shot ended an 8-0 Sixers run and trimmed Toronto's lead to nine.

He remained involved during an 11-0 burst late in the third quarter, knocking down a three and setting up Walker for a basket. Walker then made a three early in the fourth before Simons scored on the Sixers' next possession.

When Toronto pulled within six with less than five minutes remaining, Simons answered with his fifth three-pointer.

Making those shots is the most obvious way Simons can help a roster already featuring James, Joel Embiid, Tyrese Maxey and Jaylen Brown. He said the Sixers have not made him feel as though every opportunity must go in.

"They encourage us to keep shooting the ball," Simons said. "Knowing that a team has that much confidence in us to keep shooting makes the game that much easier. Whether you miss or make, as long as we get the right shots in the right moments, I think everybody can live with the misses and makes."

Simons spent seven seasons in Portland before playing last year with Boston and Chicago. His move to Philadelphia reunited him with Walker and Rayan Rupert, another former Blazer who joined the Sixers on a two-way contract during the offseason.

Knowing familiar faces awaited him helped Simons enter another new locker room.

"It made the transition seamless," he said. "Just being able to have some comfortability with guys that I played with for multiple years. It's been fun, kind of feeling like a little bit of old times. Me, Bari and Rups have been through a lot."

Walker's path to Philadelphia began a year earlier and required an additional step.

After playing 188 games over three seasons with Portland, Walker signed a two-way contract with the Sixers in July 2025. He earned a standard contract in February and has since pushed his way into the backup-center conversation despite standing 6-foot-7.

Walker believes some of the work he did on losing teams was easily missed.

"When I first got to the league, I was part of a rebuilding process," he said. "I just felt like some of the little things I did didn't always get noticed when you're losing. I told myself, if I ever got to be part of a winning organization, then I'd go out and expand my abilities."

Rebounding has made Walker difficult for Nick Nurse to overlook.

Walker credited his timing and strong hands to lessons passed down by his father, former NBA center Samaki Walker. Those instincts have become especially useful while the Sixers piece together their frontcourt behind Embiid.

"Rebounding is a skill I kind of honed in on," Walker said. "My dad was a good rebounder. He was known for his rebounding and his timing. I think it's just a gift that he transferred to me."

Walker has made it clear that he expected to earn a role this season.

"I don't know if I was delusional, but I always felt like I was going to play and I was going to be a part," he said. "I read something where they said it's a surprise, but if you were around me this summer, it wouldn't be a surprise. This is expected, and I just want to continue to get better."

The freedom Simons once had in Portland is no longer necessary. Walker does not need a high volume of touches, either. Both understand that playing beside the Sixers' stars requires shooting when open, moving the ball and handling the less glamorous work.

"You've got to find ways to impact the game multiple ways, even if you're not scoring," Simons said. "Whether it's cutting, making the right read and pass to Joel, being the right swing pass to VJ, boxing out on defense or just being in the right position."

Their opportunities will fluctuate. Simons may take nine shots one night and only a few the next. Walker's minutes will depend on matchups and the health of Philadelphia's frontcourt.

Winning has changed what they are being asked to do. Their three years together in Portland taught them why the adjustment is worthwhile.

"You feel appreciative of the times where you go into a situation where your role might be a little bit less, but you're winning," Simons said. "That's something you can't take for granted."

#2607. Back-to-back losses knock Lane Kiffin and Kentucky out of College Football Playoff contention

Kentucky and LSU played their way out of the College Football Playoff with consecutive losses.

The No. 13 Wildcats and 24th-ranked Tigers suffered their third and fourth losses of the season, respectively, Saturday night in Southeastern Conference action.

Unranked Florida, one of the most up-and-down teams in the country, dealt Kentucky a second straight loss, 21-14 in Lexington. The Cats lost last week at Tennessee.

Arch Manning threw a touchdown pass with 3 seconds remaining, rallying No. 8 Texas to a 22-21 win against slightly favored LSU in Baton Rouge. The Tigers and coach Lane Kiffin lost to Alabama last week at home.

Those setbacks should be enough to knock Kentucky (7-3, 5-3 SEC) and LSU (6-4, 3-4) out of CFP contention for good. The updated rankings will be revealed Tuesday night. The Wildcats entered the weekend at No. 11 in the CFP, 10 spots ahead of the Tigers who would have made a significant jump by beating Texas.

No. 1 Georgia, third-ranked Notre Dame, No. 9 Tennessee, 10th-ranked Texas Tech, No. 12 BYU, 16th-ranked Iowa and No. 18 Oregon enjoyed comfortable victories in Week 11.

The Bulldogs scored the first 31 points against Missouri and won 48-21 for their third consecutive lopsided victory. The Fighting Irish beat Boston College 41-7. The Volunteers won 22-7 at reeling Texas A&M. The Red Raiders scored the first 21 points and cruised past Oklahoma State, 52-27. The Cougars beat Baylor 28-7. Iowa handled Purdue by the same score. And the Ducks kept alive their slim chances of making the CFP with a 31-7 victory against Michigan.

Miami and Wake Forest are headed for a rematch.

The ACC front-runners are closing in on the Atlantic Coast Conference championship game, which would be their second meeting of the season. They played in mid-September, with the Hurricanes winning 33-20 in South Florida.

No. 5 Miami bounced back from a 31-24 loss at Notre Dame and handled Duke at home Saturday, tying a school record with its 11th consecutive ACC victory.

No. 11 Wake Forest, meanwhile, notched one of the more surprising wins of the season, thumping SMU 49-7 in Dallas as a slight underdog. It ended the Mustangs' 10-game winning streak at home and was the kind of lopsided outcome that should vault the Demon Deacons into the 12-team College Football Playoff bracket.

Arizona State can celebrate its longest day long into the night.

The Sun Devils held a team meeting Saturday at 6 a.m. MST in Tempe, Arizona, and then boarded a flight to Orlando, Florida. They landed after noon EST, arrived at the Bounce House a few hours later and then dominated UCF from the opening kickoff in a 26-13 win.

"There are no excuses," ASU coach Kenny Dillingham said. "Just spot the ball and play your best football game, and our guys responded. I'm so proud of those guys."

Cardae Mack led the way for Arizona State, finishing with 111 yards rushing and a touchdown.

The Sun Devils faced arguably the most daunting challenge in college football after the Federal Aviation Administration grounded flights nationwide for several hours Friday.

Many schools — including Utah, Texas and Tennessee — scrambled to figure things out. And conferences and TV partners helped by juggling start times.

ASU, meanwhile, agreed to travel and play on the same day — a rarity for major college programs.

"Our guys just keep bouncing back," Dillingham said. "They keep fighting. They keep punching, and that's what this program is about, and that's what these guys are about. That's what this culture is about."

Five other college teams — Baylor, Florida Atlantic, Kansas State, Minnesota and Utah — also traveled and played Saturday. They were a combined 1-4, with Utah rallying to win at Arizona and remain one of two unbeatens (along with UCLA) in major college football.

No. 19 Mississippi defended the need to postpone its game at Oklahoma until Sunday.

While numerous teams maneuvered schedules to make games happen, the Rebels were unable to get out of Oxford, Mississippi, on time, and the SEC forced Oklahoma to reschedule the game. The decision drew the ire of Sooners athletic director Roger Denny, who said late Friday it wasn't "fair to our athletes" or fans but "we've been given no other choice" after "the wrong outcome was reached."

Ole Miss responded Saturday, pointing to charter issues, flight crew issues and not wanting to bus eight or more hours.

"We regret that the game had to be moved, but we took every reasonable action in our power to avoid this scenario," the school said.

Ohio State's Jeremiah Smith became the Big Ten's career receiving yardage leader — the latest record for the uber-talented junior.

Smith finished with 117 yards and a touchdown on 11 receptions in the 21st-ranked Buckeyes' 28-19 victory against Northwestern. He now has 3,875 yards receiving, passing Purdue's John Standeford's previous league record in the second quarter.

He also tied Purdue's David Bell and Michigan's Braylon Edwards with his 17th 100-yard game.

Grant Wilson was ready to start a coaching career at Indiana this season. Then the NCAA granted him a seventh year of eligibility.

The 25-year-old Wilson threw for 305 yards, with two touchdowns and an interception, in his first start at Indiana as the sixth-ranked Hoosiers beat No. 15 USC 27-13. Wilson spent three years at Fordham and two at Old Dominion before landing at IU.

He filled in for injured starter Josh Hoover (shoulder) and delivered the play of the game: a 42-yard TD pass to Charlie Becker in the fourth quarter.

#2604. Sixers, Brown have a ‘humbling' night in loss to Celtics

Sixers, Brown have a 'humbling' night in loss to Celtics originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia

Whatever Jaylen Brown and the Sixers dreamed up for their first matchup against the Celtics soon flew out the window on Tuesday night.

Brown was whistled for two early fouls, the Sixers fell behind and their early-season flaws were on full display in a 123-101 loss at Xfinity Mobile Arena.

"We've just got to get better," Brown said. "Tonight was humbling. We got outplayed, out-executed. So we go back to the drawing board and get ready for the next one."

Over 26 minutes, Brown had 13 points on 4-for-9 shooting and five rebounds against the team that traded him away this summer.

As for the endless dissection of his relationship with former co-star Jayson Tatum, Brown didn't have much to add Tuesday. There was no public reconciliation, no obvious on-court animosity and generally nothing to satisfy fans hoping for some kind of fireworks on that front.

"I'm just focused on doing what's best for my team," Brown said. "Everything else … to be honest, I wasn't paying attention. But credit to Jayson; he played well tonight. Credit to the Celtics. They executed, they shot the hell out of the ball and they were the better team tonight."

Tatum scored 21 points, two of which came on a third-quarter slam over LeBron James. Paul George continued his fantastic start as a Celtic by dropping 36 points and draining six three-pointers.

The Celtics dominated from beyond the arc, shooting 22 for 49 (44.9 percent). The Sixers went just 11 for 37 (29.7 percent) on another night of underwhelming offense. The team sits 22nd in the NBA in offensive rating, 24th in three-point makes per game and 21st in three-point percentage.

"I think that we've got some guys that are obviously shooting much lower percentages than their last season or their career average — almost a handful of guys," Sixers head coach Nick Nurse said. "And I don't think it's because they're shooting fallaway, totally contested ones. I think they're shots we want them to take. So I think they'll continue to take 'em and I'm pretty sure those will even out into their career averages."

Joel Embiid is at 37 percent from the floor and 4 for 33 from three-point range (12.1 percent).

The Sixers' seven-time All-Star center got through an injury scare when he rolled his ankle late in the second quarter and hit a three early in the third. It was his first long-range make since the Sixers' home opener back on Oct. 22.

"It's a work in progress," Embiid said. "I think the biggest thing is just not thinking. I'm probably overthinking it. The rhythm of the game is different. I'm so used to having to create for myself, so it's a little bit different.

"But I think I'm slowly getting better. You could see as soon as I made a three, the next shot in the short corner … I didn't even think about it. I just shot it and let it fly, and I made it. … I think it's just about taking what's in front of you. Make or miss, keep working on your game. It's going to get there at some point."

Even with the Sixers second in the Eastern Conference standings at 9-3, Embiid believes the team's defense has "slacked off a little bit" in recent games.

"I don't really look at the record," he said. "I just look at the process of, 'Are we getting better every day?' We can always do a better job at all phases of the game."

"They're one of the top teams in the league and they've been together for a while," Brown said. "We've got a lot to work on over here, so we've got to get to work."

The Sixers will face the Raptors on Thursday night in Philadelphia.

They'll have to wait until Jan. 21 in Boston to see the Celtics again.

"I was looking forward to this," Brown said. "I was looking forward to playing well, but s— happens. Just get ready for the next one."

#2602. 'Pakistan fans were chanting Sehwag, Sehwag': Aaryavir's big revelation to father after U19 Asia Cup win

Aaryavir Sehwag has spoken about the nerves he felt during India's 2026 Under-19 Asia Cup final against Pakistan, revealing that he kept chanting 'Sita Ram, Sita Ram' to calm himself down. The young batter shared the moment during a video call with his father, former India cricketer Virender Sehwag, who posted their conversation on social media after India's title win."Papa, I was so nervous… was just chanting Sita Ram, Sita Ram!" Aaryavir told his father while recalling the tense moments of the final.Sharing the video, Virender said such moments meant more to him than awards and trophies."From winning Player of the Tournament to recalling those nail-biting final moments, a very special conversation with beta Aaryavir. Some moments are bigger than awards, runs and trophies. These are the memories a father will cherish forever. May you always keep your feet firmly on the ground and touch the skies with your hardwork and talent," he wrote.Aaryavir scored 58 off 61 balls in India's chase of 338 against Pakistan in the final in Oman on Saturday. India secured the title with a last-ball four from Mohit Ulva. Aaryavir was named Player of the Tournament after scoring 361 runs in five matches at an average of 90.25 and a strike rate of over 95. His tally included one century and three half-centuries. He also hit 16 sixes, the most in the tournament, and scored half-centuries in both the semi-final and final.In the video shared by Virender, Aaryavir also recalled the final over, when India needed eight runs with one wicket remaining. He said chanting 'Sitaram' helped him deal with the pressure. He also told his father that Pakistani supporters had chanted 'Sehwag' 'Sehwag' while he was batting. Virender is known for his performances in Pakistan, including scoring India's first Test triple century in Multan.

Pakistan, who were asked to bat first, posted 337/9. Usman Khan top-scored with 107 off 111 balls, hitting 11 fours and three sixes. Abdul Qadir made 80 off 54 balls, including three fours and eight sixes, while Farhan Yousaf scored 63 off 60 balls, with four boundaries and three sixes.India began their chase with an opening stand of 95 between captain Lakshya Raichandani and Aaryavir. Raichandani scored 80 off 101 balls, hitting five fours, while Aaryavir made 58 off 61 balls, including nine fours.However, India lost wickets in quick succession and slipped to 252/8. Manal Chauhan and Mohit Ulva then added 67 runs to bring India back into the contest. Manal scored 47 off 32 balls, with three fours and three sixes. After his dismissal, Mohit remained unbeaten on 49 off 26 balls, hitting five fours and three sixes, while Chigurupati Venkata contributed an unbeaten 11 to help India complete the chase.

#2600. Michael Porter Jr. sits for personal reasons — but he should be back soon

MEMPHIS, Tenn. — The Nets had to play without their leading scorer Saturday, as Michael Porter Jr. sat on the bench in street clothes.

He watched his team take a 129-110 beating in Memphis at FedExForum.

Porter wasn't injured but was a healthy scratch for personal reasons.

Michael Porter Jr. (17) of the Brooklyn Nets shoots against the Atlanta Hawks during a game at State Farm Arena in Atlanta on Saturday, Nov. 7, 2026. NBAE via Getty Images

Two sources — one a team source and another close to the player — said the issue was believed to be resolved and Porter shouldn't miss extended time.

Initially listed as questionable, Porter was ruled out an hour before tipoff.

"A personal situation came up as we were coming to the arena. So that's why it was announced late," Fernández said.

Porter is averaging a team-high 21.5 points on 45.6 percent shooting and 37.5 percent from deep. An Eastern Conference scout who spoke with The Post pointed out how easy the Nets are to defend without his unblockable shot. Julius Randle — Brooklyn's other proven veteran scorer — said others simply have to pick up the slack.

"Everybody has to step in and chip in. It's not just one person," Randle said. "So we've all got to step up and chip in and do it collectively as a unit."

Day'Ron Sharpe (16 points, 11 rebounds, five assists) had his third double-double of the season already. His career high is six in 2023-24.

Brooklyn Nets head coach Jordi Fernandez gestures from the sideline in the second half of an NBA basketball game against the Memphis Grizzlies in Memphis, Tenn. AP Photo/Brandon Dill

Fernández handed Noah Clowney the start at small forward for Porter. With Randle, Sharpe, Egor Dëmin and Danny Wolf, every Nets starter was at least 6-foot-9 or taller, just as they had been in the blowout win in New Orleans three nights earlier.

This was the first time any NBA team had started a lineup of players all 6-foot-9 or taller since the Los Angeles Lakers had done so April 21, 1990.

Mikel Brown Jr. and Nolan Traore both returned after having missed the blowout win in New Orleans three nights earlier. It marked just the third game that the Nets have had Dëmin, Brown and Traore together.

Fernández said Brown is still on his minutes limit. With Wolf still starting at two-guard, Brown and Traore logged just 19 minutes each.

The Nets got thrown into travel chaos Friday by the Federal Aviation Administration's decision to ground every flight nationwide for four hours. They were already set to board their flight but had to stay overnight in New Orleans and fly to Memphis at 9 a.m.

"Yeah, obviously it was something that we couldn't control," Fernández said. "And to be honest with you, it was not that bad. We had good rest and got here [Saturday] morning and did our walk-through, and probably [would have] gone to the gym, but we were not able to. And I think we feel good and ready to go."

#2598. Big Ten power rankings after Week 11: USC moves down after loss

The race for a spot in the Big Ten Championship, and subsequently the College Football Playoff, is heating up, and we're seeing some monumental matchups across the league as we get deep into November.

It was the USC Trojans and Indiana Hoosiers who had the headline matchup on Saturday, with Curt Cignetti sending Lincoln Riley packing, a result that led to the Trojans sliding in our power rankings once again. We also saw Dan Lanning's Oregon Ducks pick up another big win, this time over the Michigan Wolverines, while the Ohio State Buckeyes outlast the Northwestern Wildcats, and the Maryland Terrapins got a big upset win over the Wisconsin Badgers.

With two weeks of regular-season play remaining, the next couple of weeks will be fascinating as teams jockey for position and try to grab the two spots in the Big Ten championship game.

Here are our Big Ten Power Rankings after Week 8:

Analysis: Every time it seems like Rutgers has hit rock bottom, they find a way to dig deeper. Another blowout loss isn't a shock, but the fact that Rutgers came out and announced that Greg Schiano would be sticking around for next season was a surprise. I'm not sure what else the Scarlet Knights are hoping to see from him, but the misery is continuing in Piscataway.

Analysis: This Purdue is a far cry from the September firepower we saw earlier this season. Ryan Browne was ineffective all night, and there was no light in the defense either. It's been a strange season for the Boilermakers, and it's tough to see another win on the schedule.

Analysis: Maryland, even with a backup quarterback, has some momentum suddenly. It's too little, too late, of course, but Cardell Williams did enough to help the Terrapins pull off a surprising win at home, and the pass rush closed out the game. There are some pieces on the roster that are revealing themselves as must-keep players for whoever takes over as head coach. Looking at you, Brian Kelly.

Analysis: Michigan State's defense seems to be finding some things that are working, but the uncertainty at quarterback and injuries to key playmakers on offense make the Spartans very similar to their in-state counterparts, Michigan. Things need to break right for the offense to have success, and much of that is reliant on the defense forcing turnovers. There was some momentum in the first half, but the Huskies clamped down in the second half and didn't provide many opportunities. The Spartans' depth is running thin at several positions.

Analysis: Minnesota has played up or down to its competition for most of the season. Given the disappointing season Penn State has had, the Golden Gophers appeared ready to match a dud performance, but they once again got stomped at the line of scrimmage and let the Nittany Lions toy with them on the ground. The rollercoaster season for PJ Fleck continues.

Analysis: Talk about a dejected team. Michigan only showed some energy after a long drive to end the third quarter, danced during "Shout!" and was then turned away at the goal line. The experiment of playing both Tommy Carr and Bryce Underwood was odd, as they swapped out without much rhyme or reason, and although the Wolverines rushed for 200 yards, 70 of it came on one play. The vaunted defense was finally tested downfield, and it broke. Kyle Whittingham's seat was already warm, and the eject button might be getting pushed soon.

Analysis: Wisconsin couldn't contain a backup quarterback that was thrust into action at the last minute. That speaks to the peaks and valleys of this season for the Badgers. Maryland has been without direction for months, and yet when it needed to the most, Maryland was able to throw on the Badgers' defense and get a late stop. Ryan Hopkins and Colton Joseph are clearly not up to the task of leading the offense, and there isn't enough talent up front to support a run game. It looked like a high school product at times, and the season has officially gone off the rails in Madison.

Analysis: For the first time in a month, Nebraska ran the ball well with both Jamal Rule and Anthony Colandrea, which opened up some of the intermediate passing opportunities for the veteran quarterback. The Cornhuskers' offense got a boost from the coordinator change, but facing the Rutgers defense is also a good cure for offensive woes. It was a step in the right direction, but Nebraska has much bigger fish to fry moving forward with Ohio State and Iowa left on the schedule.

Week 11 Result: 21-14 Win vs. Michigan State

Analysis: Washington tried to give the game away with a muffed punt in the fourth quarter, but the defense did stand tall in the second half and forced the Spartans to put together long drives if they wanted to win. Demond Williams did damage in the first half, but much of his yardage came on the final drive of the game that led to the winning touchdown, and the Huskies were otherwise quiet. Inconsistency on offense has plagued Washington all season, and it was on display on Saturday. The Huskies did earn bowl eligibility at the right time, with both Indiana and Oregon left on the schedule.

Analysis: Looking at the final score and watching how Katin Houser played, it's pretty remarkable that the Illini had a chance to win. Houser tossed three picks and should have had even more, but the rainy conditions probably helped him out a little bit. The offensive line was no match for UCLA's blitz packages, and the early big plays the Bruins hit were never answered. Illinois has a tough finish to the season coming up with Iowa and Northwestern left.

Analysis: Penn State continued to establish its identity on the ground with big days from Carson Hansen and Cam Wallace. The defense sacked Drake Lindsey three times and forced incompletions with pressure. Rocco Becht played through injury and capitalized when he did get to throw the ball, which wasn't often. It might have taken nearly a full season, but the Nittany Lions now know how this team can win offensively, and they could rise to eight wins to finish the regular season with just Rutgers and Maryland left on the schedule.

Analysis: Missing Aidan Chiles has really hurt Northwestern the past two weeks. The offense as a whole hasn't changed much, but his playmaking and ability to open rushing lanes have completely changed the unit's effectiveness. Northwestern doesn't have the athletes defensively to go toe-to-toe with Ohio State, and although a late score dressed up the final score, the Wildcats were playing catch-up throughout. Northwestern does have two winnable games to end the season, but Chiles' health is the biggest factor moving forward.

Week 11 Result: 28-19 Win vs. Northwestern

Analysis: The Buckeyes decided to throw it to Jeremiah Smith this week, and to nobody's surprise, that was a winning formula. He set more records and topped 100 yards with a touchdown again, and Ohio State cruised to a win. The Buckeyes picked up five sacks and flustered the Northwestern offense for much of the day and were always in control, even if the scoreboard looked somewhat close.

Analysis: USC's playoff dreams are likely finished with another loss on the road in a big game. Jayden Maiava played one of his worst games, tossing three interceptions. The Trojans got down inside the 30-yard line six times, but only managed 13 points thanks to turnovers and missed field goals. The Lincoln Riley question continues to loom large, but it will be interesting to see how hard the team plays in the final two games.

Analysis: It's still odd to think that Iowa has a couple of star pass-catchers, but Braeden Jackson is a difference-maker on offense and special teams, and Tony Diaz is the gadget man that the Hawkeyes are always trying to get the ball to. Jackson and Diaz both scored against Purdue and helped Hank Brown remain efficient on a big day for the offense. The Hawkeyes know how to control the clock and should be able to run the ball to victory in their final two games, but they have a reliable passing attack, finally. Iowa does need some help to get to the conference championship game.

Analysis: Oregon is playing to its potential right now, even without Dante Moore. Dylan Raiola is playing the best ball of his life, Dakorien Moore is breaking into superstar territory, and the defense is playing complementary football. The Ducks weren't afraid to test a talented Michigan defense vertically, and they let their athletes win. Oregon has a short turnaround this week heading on the road to Michigan State, but it's very reasonable to see the Ducks winning out and potentially backing into an at-large bid for the playoff.

Analysis: Hello, Grant Wilson. The Hoosiers didn't need Josh Hoover, as Wilson got the start and threw for 305 yards and two touchdowns, and he had time to operate thanks to a potent rushing attack in front of him. Indiana does have something of a quarterback conundrum on its hands whenever Hoover gets healthy. The Indiana defense is the story, however, applying pressure throughout and making USC's offense collapse in on itself. Indiana has the indie track to the Big Ten title game, with a trip to Washington and a home date against Purdue remaining.

Analysis: UCLA ground out another win with Ty Dieffenbach, although it once again was not pretty. Dieffenbach played through injury after briefly leaving the game before halftime. Most of his damage came in the first half, and Aidan Mizell has emerged as his favorite target downfield. As a result of the reliance on the big passing plays, the run game, which was the Bruins' calling card to start the season, has struggled to be as consistent. The tailbacks averaged just 3.2 yards per carry. The Bruins will be tested in the trenches the next two weeks at Michigan and at home against USC.

#2596. Nets can’t overcome slow start in 129-110 loss to Grizzlies

Those are words you never want to hear from the head coach of a rebuilding team. Especially not in Year 3.

The Brooklyn Nets had a chance to build on their blowout win over New Orleans. Mikel Brown Jr. was back after missing the last two games. There was a small window to finally pick up some momentum. Instead, they followed it up with another frustrating loss, 129-110, in the finale of a four-game road-trip.

Brooklyn fell behind early and trailed 38-23 after the first quarter. You'd never think Memphis played a game just the night before.

The Nets struggled to contain Memphis from the perimeter and committed 16 turnovers that led to 30 Grizzlies points. They made a push in the third quarter and cut a 23-point deficit to eight, but couldn't get the stops necessary to make it a game.

"I think we cut it to seven at some point and you should have been in the game, but we are not mature enough… we played against a team that played in a second of a back-to-back with the same travel that we had, and they played the right way, played really hard and we're not there yet. So, you know, go back and work and find ways to get better, because when you're not consistent and you don't find those ways, it's just like that's not what we want to do here," Fernandez said after the game.

The Nets briefly led 7-5, but Memphis responded with a 9-0 run and never let up control. Cedric Coward, Cam Spencer and Jaylen Wells got hot early, and a Wells' three-pointer forced a Brooklyn timeout with 7:55 remaining in the first quarter, with the Grizzlies flipping the score to 16-9 in their own favor.

The shooting didn't slow down. Memphis made nine three-pointers in the opening quarter and carried a 38-23 lead into the second. Brooklyn faced a 19-point deficit in the first half before making a small dent in it. The Grizzlies still led 71-54 at halftime.

"Right now the two practices we've had, we've practiced very well. So we practice better than we play, which is not a terrible sign. It's a frustrating sign because you believe you're better, but all we can do is go back to work."

Julius Randle said Brooklyn didn't match Memphis' urgency from the opening tip. The three-time All-Star pointed to the team's overall start as a bigger issue.

"We didn't punch first. We didn't come out with a sense of urgency, and they took advantage of that," he said.

"Just organization. I think maybe just trying too hard, playing a little unorganized, stuff like that," Randle said. "And then just attention to detail, you know, just think we got a lapse of focus sometimes."

Sparked by scoring from Noah Clowney, Day'Ron Sharpe, and Julius Randle, Brooklyn put together a strong third-quarter surge to cut the deficit to 85-77 with 5:12 remaining. Memphis took a 103-84 lead into the fourth quarter and eventually stretched the margin beyond 20.

It was Brooklyn's fifth loss by double figures.

"They got to grow fast," Fernandez said about the young group. "You know, like being 20 is not an excuse.…. I'm frustrated or I get mad because I know they're very good and they're better than this. And when I just don't see a connected group is, it hurts…"

Michael Porter Jr. attended Saturday's game after missing time for personal reasons. Fernández was asked about Porter's absence and whether he knew when the forward might return, but the coach declined.

Mikel Brown Jr. returned after missing the last two games. It's been a bit of a strange start and the guard missed the last two games for two different reasons — one for injury management and the other for an illness. The rookie finished with six points and two assists on 2-of-5 shooting in 20 minutes.

After the game, his father pointed out the importance of the floor general. Take it for whatever it's worth.

Brooklyn's trip to Memphis didn't go according to plan. The Nets were caught in Friday night's FAA ground stop after boarding their charter flight out of New Orleans, forcing the team to stay overnight before finally flying out Saturday morning.

The team arrived in Memphis around 11 a.m., just hours before its game against the Grizzlies. The unexpected delay also forced Brooklyn to scrap its planned morning shootaround.

"Yeah, I mean, obviously it was something that we couldn't control," head coach Jordi Fernández said. "And to be honest with you, it was not that bad. We had good rest and got here [Saturday] morning and did our walkthrough, and probably [would have] gone to the gym, but we were not able to. And I think we feel good and ready to go."

Fernández acknowledged that the altered schedule wasn't ideal, particularly for players who had grown accustomed to the team's usual pregame routine.

"Everybody's safe. It's the most important thing," he said.

The Nets are back home against the 76ers on Monday, November 16.

#2595. Alexander Ovechkin announces this will be his last NHL season: 'Let's have fun'

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

Alex Ovechkin's 22nd NHL season will be his last, the Washington Capitals superstar announced on Monday."This is gonna be my last year," Ovechkin told his teammates in a video the Capitals posted to social media. "It's sad, but it is what it is. We have an unbelievable team this year. There are 82 games left. Let's make the playoffs, and let's have fun."

Ovechkin has already established himself as the greatest goal-scorer in hockey history with 929 tallies, and he still has 82 games to add to that total before he hangs up his skates.

The No. 1 overall pick in the 2004 NHL Draft, Ovechkin immediately established himself as a prolific scorer by notching 52 goals en route to winning the Calder Trophy as a rookie.

Since then, Ovechkin has won the Rocket Richard Trophy as the NHL's leading goal-scorer a record nine times. The Capitals legend's resume also features an Art Ross Trophy and three Hart Trophy wins.

The crowning achievement in Ovechkin's illustrious career is leading Washington to its first Stanley Cup in 2017-18. After coming up short in a number of postseasons prior to that, Ovechkin led all playoff performers with 15 goals and won the Conn Smythe Trophy as a result.

Following the 2025-26 season, there was speculation that Ovechkin could retire, but he signed an incentive-laden one-year deal with the Caps.Sensing that this could be Ovechkin's final season, the Capitals loaded up to give their franchise icon one more shot at the Stanley Cup. Washington signed former Buffalo Sabres winger Alex Tuch in free agency and acquired winger Jordan Kyrou from the St. Louis Blues via trade.

No team is as loaded on the wings as the Capitals, and they have one of the best rosters in the Metro Division. Washington has the ingredients to challenge the defending Cup champion Carolina Hurricanes and get Ovechkin one more ring before he rides off into the sunset.

Through Week 6, opponents had scored touchdowns on 18 of 22 red-zone trips against Washington, yet New York left crucial points behind when Frankie Luvu punched the ball loose from Malik Nabers at the 16-yard line and Jeremy Reaves recovered.

Washington also held the Giants to 4-of-12 on third down, including two critical late stops when it couldn't afford to give New York another first down—a defensive standard that will be tested immediately when Joe Burrow and the Bengals visit Landover.

One of the biggest turnarounds from the Commanders tie back in Week 5 against the Giants and their win over the Giants on Thursday night was the plan of attack against Cover-0. In Week 5, the Giants spammed Cover-0 blitzes throughout the second half and overtime and the Commanders just couldn't handle it. They continually attempted to take shots down the field to try and hit explosive plays rather than just finding a simple quick solution.

Daniels was seeing those blitzes a lot better and it showed in the most critical moment.

Having thrown two late interceptions, it looked like the Commanders season was over, but the defense bailed Daniels out and gave him another opportunity, which he wasn't going to pass up. On third and four with under a minute remaining in the game, the Giants of course show Daniels another Cover-0 blitz. This time, Daniels doesn't adjust the protection, but instead signals to Stefon Diggs in the slot to change his route. In the first game, when Daniels saw Cover-0, he often checked into a shot play to try and attack the blitz and throw a big touchdown over the top of it. But clearly this time they were looking to play smarter, and it worked out much better for them.

Daniels adjusts Diggs route, having him run a slant against the slot corner. When he snaps the ball, the defense comes on the blitz, but the defensive tackle to the right side of the line pops up and drops out into coverage, trying to take away a hot throw over the middle. Daniels just checked into a hot throw over the middle with Diggs running a slant, so that could potentially be a problem. But Daniels does a great job adjusting his throw to beat that defensive lineman dropping into coverage.

Diggs runs a great route, beating the corner with a nice stutter move before sharply cutting across his face to get inside. The throw from Daniels has to be slightly behind him because of that defensive lineman dropping into coverage, but Diggs does well to adjust to the pass and make the grab. Diggs breaks a diving tackle from the slot corner and gets some help from fellow receiver Van Jefferson, who helps block the other nearby defender. With both defenders out of the picture, Diggs runs uncontested into the end zone for a 32-yard game-winning touchdown.

It goes to show that you can still score a big touchdown against Cover-0 without having to try and take a deep shot constantly. As I said back in Week 5, I don't mind that their philosophy against Cover-0 is to go on the attack, in fact I quite like it. It offers you one-on-one matchups and I like that they feel like they can take shots with those matchups. But they clearly went too far in Week 5 in trying to throw bombs down the field. This game proved there's more ways to go about it. Winning a one-on-one doesn't have to be 20 yards down the field, it can be a quick slant like this when you have Stefon Diggs or Antonio Williams in the slot. With it being Cover-0, if you win that one-on-one quickly, there's every chance the receiver can run freely after the catch and score as there's no safety help over the top.

So credit should go to David Blough and Jayden Daniels for making that adjustment. It's a shame they couldn't have made it back in Week 5 because they would have won that game too if they had, but it paid off for them this time around and it meant that the Commanders have just about kept their season alive.

After catching just 17 passes over his first two-plus NFL seasons behind Zach Ertz and Chig Okonkwo, third-year tight end Ben Sinnott stepped in when Okonkwo exited Thursday night's game with a back injury and delivered four receptions for 42 yards and a touchdown.

Sinnott hurdled a defender to convert a critical first down on the final drive of the first half before hauling in a go-ahead score on third-and-goal, then added a 24-yard catch-and-run early in the third quarter. He has now caught 21 of 24 career targets, making a strong case for offensive coordinator David Blough to feature more two-tight-end sets down the stretch.

In two-tight-end packages, Commanders offensive coordinator David Blough should give Sinnott a few defined passing-game opportunities on early downs and near the goal line. Blough should continue his approach of giving each tight end their own distinct role, but should also look to take advantage of Sinnott's receiving and after-the-catch ability that, until Thursday night, was going to waste.

If Okonkwo is back to his usual workload against Cincinnati, I'll be watching the snaps he shares with Sinnott. When Washington needs a first down and both tight ends are out there, does Daniels go back to Sinnott?

Brandon Aiyuk has made no secret of where he wants to resume his career, regularly appearing in Commanders gear on Instagram as he works back from his 2024 knee injury. While talk of a reunion with former Arizona State teammate Jayden Daniels grew complicated after Aiyuk's July remarks about the quarterback's mother, ESPN insider Jeremy Fowler reports that the two friends have mended their relationship.

Aiyuk has since been reinstated from the reserve/left squad list, with San Francisco holding a roster exemption through November 23 — the exact day Washington hosts Cincinnati on Monday Night Football. With Stefon Diggs set to hit free agency after the season, general manager Adam Peters may have a decision to make if the 49ers cut ties with the former All-Pro receiver.

Daniels completed 23 of 33 attempts for 249 yards and a season-high three touchdown passes. According to Next Gen Stats, all three touchdown passes came against Cover 0, a blitz-heavy design New York used successfully and often during the 27-27 Week 5 tie.

The three scores were also on passes between the numbers, a feat Daniels previously achieved once in 2024, during a Week 17 win over the Falcons. That accomplishment flies in the face of pre-draft criticism regarding a supposed allergy to throwing over the middle. Ironically, both interceptions were on throws outside the numbers.

Wherever the ball needed to go, the quarterback wasn't about to let the Commanders' season spiral further south. "I didn't want to let my team down in that moment," Daniels said, "so when they gave me another opportunity to go out there and win the game, I didn't want to let them down."

The scary part for defenses is that Daniels is starting to find a rhythm after five consecutive starts.

The Giants had one more chance to win the game down by just three points, and they were in Washington territory after a 21-yard throw to Malachi Fields. The Commanders' defense needed to make a play, and Styles called his own number with a blitz up the middle to put pressure on McCarthy.

Styles ended up hitting McCarthy in the arm as he went for a deep pass to Malik Nabers, and the throw ended up turning into a lob that CB Rasul Douglas intercepted to end the game. It's very unlikely the Commanders win this game if Styles doesn't make those two plays in critical moments, and that's just a sample of his rookie season so far.

Sonny Styles' Defensive Rookie of the Year Resume

This season's DROY award should be a tight race, but Styles has a strong resume already. His game-changing plays won't show up on the stat sheet, but his stats are just as impressive. Styles already has 80 tackles this season, which is the 7th most for a LB in the entire NFL.

He also has an interception, a forced fumble, and three pass breakups through nine games, and it's reasonable to believe that more are on the way. Styles is also a vocal leader who flashes his IQ and awareness on the field to put his team in a position to succeed.

I'm tired of watching the Eagles change offensive coordinators every year or two, only to end up dealing with the same problems.

Bad protection, predictable plays, poor adjustments, and talented players not living up to their potential.

At what point do we stop blaming execution and start looking at the people responsible for teaching these players?

Look, I'll give Nick Sirianni credit. Two Super Bowl appearances and a championship aren't accidents. But we're sitting at 2–7, and something clearly isn't working.

I don't believe firing everybody and hiring the next hot coordinator is the answer either. That's how we end up right back here two years from now.

If I'm Howie Roseman, I'm looking for coaches who can actually make players better, not just coaches who happened to work on great teams.

He's my first interview. He has actual NFL play-calling experience, helped build an effective running game in Arizona, and has coached several offensive positions.

I'd give him control of the offense and have him call plays. No more guessing who's really responsible when things go wrong.

CeeDee Lamb and Jerry Jones have used the word bittersweet this week to describe the Dallas Cowboys' season. The Cowboys owner and general manager believes his team has the personnel to be better than their 4-5 record. Somehow, though, the Cowboys are still completely in the mix to win the NFC East.

"It would just prove us right," Lamb said, "(about) how we think of ourselves throughout this building. Prediction: 49ers 27, Cowboys 17 — Jon Machota, Cowboys beat writer

Turns out, all six of Zvada's misses this season — three pushed wide right and three yanked wide left — have come from the right hash.

It is fair to say that Zvada's struggles were critical parts of why the Giants tied and lost games to the Commanders, rather than winning both games. He missed three kicks in the tie to Washington in Week 5, and his miss Thursday came in a 3-point loss.

The point here isn't to debate which decisions Harbaugh made correctly, and which he didn't. Though discussing that is certainly fair game. The point is that Zvada's continued misses are complicating the decision-making and costing the Giants points that are probably costing them games.

In an NFC East race that seems likely to go down to the wire, and where every decision, every made or missed kick, everything that happens in the margins of an NFL game, could end up making the difference how much rope can the Giants give Zvada to figure it out?
